Searle boots it into the corner.. this time it’s short but still Tigers manage to mess it up and knock on. Kemeny is being such a nuisance in there.

Mitchell gets scragged by Hamer-Webb and in the rain misses a kick attempt, as Tigers edge their way closer into Saints’ 22. The hosts are averaging only 50 per cent at the moment - Kemeny is making a real nuisance of himself and getting into Blamire’s head - and they lose another in a promising position.

Saints are knocking on Tigers’ door and Fin Smith makes some good post-contact metres as he eats up grass and edges towards Tigers’ try line. Some staunch defence from the hosts, who survive after Prowse is penalised for not rolling away.

Eeek, after his 50m hoof Steward is the first to blink in a brief kick tennis exchange and spills the ball in Tigers’ territory. Tigers collapse the scrum - they’re pushing a bit too hard before the engagement - and Saints look to work up a head of steam.

Smith asks questions with another chip over the defence but Tigers deal with it well enough and van Poortvliet fires it clear.

But Saints aren’t done, they come again and Smith looks cross field and picks out Rory Hutchinson, who is met by Hamer-Webb.

There’s a bit of spice between the pair before referee Craig Maxwell-Keys intervenes and declares it was a good contest.

Tigers have already crafted some decent opportunities in these opening exchanges but their execution has been poor, as the hosts come again - this time through Kata - but it’s Chessum who spills once more. Saints win a scrum penalty after van der Flier engages too early. Saints look to work their way down field but we’ll come back for a Tigers’ penalty after Pollock was offside from Smith’s kick.

Steward lines up a kick from 50 metres and he splits the uprights. Tigers are on the board.

He's struck that beautifully! 😍 Freddie Steward nails a penalty from halfway to get @LeicesterTigers on the board 🐯👏 📺 Stream TNT Sports on HBO Max https://t.co/ISqfkeU3vl https://t.co/opyNyxbART

Fin Smith is hobbling a little which might cause some alarm in Northampton and beyond. Hopefully nothing serious for the England stand-off. He is still able to take re-starts so that is a good sign…

Craig Maxwell-Keys, the referee, won’t be short on advice this afternoon. Two penalties to Northampton and the home crowd are already growing restless.

He is going to need eyes in the back of his head this afternoon. It took all of two minutes for the first coming-together after a thumping double hit on Fin Smith from Archie van der Flier and Olly Cracknell.

There’s something heartening primal about an East Midlands derby and this one feels like it is right on the edge. It’s a sell-out and it is intense.

Tigers respond positively by flooding Saints’ half and win a lineout deep in the red zone. It’s a huge defensive set from Saints, who manage to force their rivals back and Leicester can’t seem to make the pressure count.

Searle pokes through a cross-field grubber but there’s top much on it for Seale, but Tigers will come back for the free kick after Saints are penalised for collapsing a driving maul.

They come again but the Tigers lose it through Chessum five-metres out - it’s a very wet ball out there so we can expect to see a lot of that - and Pollock leads the celebrations among the forwards. You can bet he’ll be in their faces all afternoon.

Saints strike first! They make a mess of their first line out but Chessum manages to knock on and the visitors have a scrum in Tigers’ 22. The hosts are too eager to engage and Mitchell takes the free kick quickly. Saints edge forward with some patient phase play - they get the offside advantage and Smith chips the Tigers’ defence.

Billy Searle is tracking the ball but he’s scampering back awkwardly and completely misses the catch. Instead James Pater gathers the loose ball and watches it into his hands.. and grounds it. Saints strike first! Conversion is good.

Striking first on derby day 💥 James Pater capitalises on a Leicester error to open the scoring for @SaintsRugby 😇 📺 Stream TNT Sports on HBO Max https://t.co/ISqfkeU3vl https://t.co/kpjaHgHERp

Billy Searle gets proceedings underway and its Saints who gain some fine field position early on after the hosts are penalised for not rolling away. Fin Smith is smothered by a double-tackle and the England fly-half spills the ball. Saints don’t like it and there’s a few afters but things calm down pretty quickly. Tension already!

.. and enter what looks like a horrendously wet Welford Road. Rain is pouring - expect dropped balls and greasy conditions!

Our rugby reporter Charles Richardson relieves the time Manu Tuilagi gave one - or a few - to Chris Ashton back in 2011.

In a fiery – when is this fixture not? – first half, both were sin-binned for their involvement in what might be described as a disagreement.

Tuilagi took Ashton out, slightly high, off the ball as the wing attempted to support scrum-half Lee Dickson’s quickly taken penalty. Ashton then gave the 19-year-old, uncapped Tuilagi a little shove on the floor, before the red mist descended on the future England centre. Catch the full read here.

Henry Pollock’s cornrow phase is over. He’s sporting a mousy mop for today’s East Midlands derby.

The Northampton No 8 - currently warming up in a snood - will be pantomime-villain-in-chief for the Saints in these parts but he has a big afternoon ahead.

This is exactly the sort of occasion and arm wrestle which he needs to excel in to prove to Steve Borthwick he is worth more than a bench role for England next month.

Wrapped up against the storm ⛈️ It's wet and windy ahead of the East Midlands derby - just ask Henry Pollock! 😅 📺 Stream TNT Sports on HBO Max https://t.co/ISqfkeU3vl https://t.co/1pirJ1Nm2D

Leicester were buoyed in the week by re-signing Jack van Poortfliet, who extended his contract with his boyhood club.

I grew up supporting Leicester, it’s always been my club,” said the England scrum half. This place feels like home in my rugby life. The club is in a really good position, I think we have a great group of lads and great coaches.

I love playing rugby here, I have my best mates here and I believe that we’ve got a group of lads that we can do great things with. I want to be in a place that I love playing for and I believe can win trophies.”

Squally conditions this afternoon at Mattioli Welford Road - in fact make that horrible. An interesting test then for Northampton as lovers of the beautiful game.

You would imagine that the rain and wind would suit a Leicester side whose DNA is set piece power better.

Expect the catch and drive to get plenty of game time and Jack van Poortvliet and Billy Searle to go to the air regularly. It could be a stern examination for teenage Saints full-back James Pater.

It’s a big day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Liverpool are facing renewed interest from Bayern Munich in Florian Wirtz and Rio Ngumoha as the German giants prepare for the possibility of losing Michael Olise or Jamal Musiala.

Bayern are assessing several attacking options across Europe, with Manchester City winger Jérémy Doku also featuring on their shortlist.

However, convincing Liverpool to part with two players who could have an enormous influence on the club’s future under Andoni Iraola will be particularly difficult.

According to TEAMtalk, Bayern are maintaining a strong interest in Wirtz and Ngumoha as uncertainty surrounds the futures of Olise and Musiala.

The German champions have yet to finalise a contract extension with Olise, who has attracted interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Bayern’s admiration for Wirtz dates back to his Bayer Leverkusen days, while Ngumoha’s rapid development has caught the attention of their recruitment department.

Both Liverpool players scored and provided an assist during Sunday’s impressive 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

However, Bayern’s chances of signing Ngumoha could soon suffer a significant setback.

A recent CaughtOffside report revealed that Liverpool are close to finalising a new long-term contract for the 18-year-old winger amid growing interest from European heavyweights.

Bayern are also monitoring Doku, despite the Belgian international signing a contract extension with Manchester City until 2031 earlier this year.

Liverpool should firmly resist any approach for either player.

Wirtz is beginning to demonstrate why the Reds invested so heavily in bringing him to Anfield, with Iraola seemingly helping the German international rediscover his confidence and attacking influence.

Ngumoha, meanwhile, represents exactly the type of emerging talent Liverpool should be building around rather than cashing in on.

The teenager’s fearless approach, explosive acceleration and ability to unsettle defenders make him an exciting long-term prospect.

Bayern’s interest is understandable, but their recruitment problems should not become Liverpool’s concern.

Securing Ngumoha to an improved contract and continuing to build the attack around Wirtz should be straightforward priorities for the Anfield hierarchy.

At 18 and 23 respectively, the pair could potentially form the foundation of Liverpool’s attack for much of the next decade.

Selling either player would undermine that vision, regardless of how financially attractive Bayern’s eventual proposals might be.

#1243. Supporter Travel Update: Everton v Coventry

Everton and Merseyrail are providing supporters with an early update on travel arrangements ahead of the Premier League fixture against Coventry City at Hill Dickinson Stadium, which will now take place on Friday 6 November, kick-off 8pm (GMT).

The fixture will take place while significant, pre-planned and essential engineering works are still under way across parts of the local rail network, with those works due to conclude over the course of that weekend. As a result, normal matchday travel arrangements are expected to be affected.

Merseyrail has been working closely with Everton, Liverpool City Region Combined Authority and other transport partners for a number of months to plan for the works and minimise disruption to supporters and other passengers.

The move of the Coventry fixture into this period means supporters attending the game should expect changes to the usual public transport options available for travel to and from Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Detailed travel advice is currently being developed, including information on rail services, replacement transport where applicable and alternative ways of travelling to and from the stadium.

Supporters do not need to make any changes to their travel plans at this stage. Detailed information will be provided well in advance of the fixture as arrangements are confirmed.

With the match taking place on a Friday evening, supporters will also be encouraged to allow additional time for their journey and to check the latest travel information before setting off.

Everton and Merseyrail recognise the importance of providing supporters with clear and timely information and will continue to work together, alongside the Liverpool City Region Combined Authority and other transport partners, to support safe and effective travel to and from the fixture.

Further updates will be published through evertonfc.com, Merseyrail channels and Liverpool City Region transport information services as arrangements are confirmed.

Manchester United are facing growing uncertainty over Bruno Fernandes’ future after Juventus joined AC Milan in expressing interest in signing the Portuguese midfielder next summer.

The 32-year-old has temporarily put contract negotiations on hold, preferring to concentrate on helping United recover from their disappointing start to the Premier League season under new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

However, the lack of progress over a new agreement has encouraged some of Europe’s biggest clubs to explore the possibility of signing him.

According to Italian publication Tuttosport, Juventus are monitoring Fernandes’ contract situation with a view to potentially signing him without a transfer fee next summer.

AC Milan are also interested, with manager Ruben Amorim keen on reuniting with his former Manchester United captain. The pair share the same representative agency, potentially giving Milan an advantage in future negotiations.

Fernandes is already familiar with Italian football, having previously represented Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria before returning to Portugal.

A recent CaughtOffside report revealed that Fernandes has reportedly rejected United’s last two contract proposals, leaving negotiations at a standstill.

However, Man United retain the option to extend his existing agreement until 2028, meaning a free transfer next summer is far from guaranteed.

Losing Fernandes would represent an enormous setback for United, particularly during such an important rebuilding period.

Despite being 32, the Portuguese international remains one of the team’s most influential players, offering creativity, leadership and goals from midfield.

United should understandably consider his age when discussing a long-term extension, but allowing a player of his quality to leave without receiving a transfer fee would make little financial or sporting sense.

The responsibility now falls on Pochettino and the club’s hierarchy to demonstrate that United are moving in the right direction.

Fernandes has previously turned down opportunities to leave Old Trafford, but his loyalty should not be taken for granted.

Juventus and Milan could offer an attractive alternative if United’s struggles continue.

Activating his contract extension would provide temporary security, but convincing Fernandes that he can still compete for major honours in Manchester should remain the ultimate priority.

#1239. The eight players that should be on Man United's January list to turn season around - even with paltry £50m budget: From a goalscorer available for just £7m to star desperate to reunite with Mauricio Pochettino and a flying left back

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026

Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.

While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.

As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, United plan to spend less than £50million, with two additions targeted, one of which could be on loan.

Should United, currently 19th, remain in the bottom three by the time the window opens on January 1, there is a slim chance they go big in a desperate bid to guarantee their Premier League status.

But for now, the watchword inside United is discipline, and that means any recruitment will have to be more creative than ever before.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the transfer landscape and assesses eight players – a mix of Premier League proven and some lesser-known quantities – who could fit United’s needs AND their budget…

Mauricio Pochettino needs recruits in January - although Man United's budget being below £50m won't help his cause

Brentford centre back Nathan Collins is one of United's top targets, but he won't be available on the cheap

Position: Centre back, Age: 25, Club: Brentford

Signing Premier League proven players is absolutely the preference of the United hierarchy, as evidenced by their recent business. Six of their past eight arrivals joined with experience in the division under their belt.

Collins is one of the club’s top targets for the winter window. The 25-year-old Brentford captain would bring leadership, an aerial presence and is comfortable as a ball carrier from the back, which Pochettino values.

Collins is seen as having many of the same attributes that Harry Maguire has brought to United over the years. And while he is not a flash name, he is viewed as a player that can immediately deliver some solidity.

Highly durable and a threat at set-pieces, Brentford won’t be willing to part with their captain, who is under contract until 2029, on the cheap.

Signing Collins would eat up most of the budget – but United are not deterred.

Position: Left back, Age: 25, Club: Man City

United made a late play to land the Algerian on loan in January, only for City to tell them they would only sanction a permanent exit. In the end, time ran out and Ait-Nouri stayed put.

He has started just one game in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and is yet to feature at all in the Premier League this season. His situation is unlikely to improve in the near future, either.

A loan with an obligation to buy could suit all parties here, even if sending Ait-Nouri to their fiercest rivals may be difficult for City to stomach.

Rayan Ait-Nouri (right) has fallen out of favour under Enzo Maresca and is yet to play a minute in the Premier League this season. Could he make a move across Manchester?

Position: Left back, Age: 27, Club: Crystal Palace

An intriguing option given United have been keeping tabs on Mitchell for over a year.

Palace are quite secretive when it comes to Mitchell – they kept his last contract extension under wraps – but as it stands, his deal is set to expire at the end of the season.

Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace. The same is true of Fulham's Calvin Bassey, but sources are increasingly sceptical about United's chances of signing him in January.

For all of Palace’s struggles, Mitchell is proven at this level and would likely hit the ground running. The fact United are not his only suitor is a sign they aren’t straying down a blind alley.

With the 27-year-old’s contract yet to be extended and big clubs sniffing around, he could prove to be this January’s Marc Guehi should United nip in ahead of Liverpool, with Reds boss Andoni Iraola also keen.

Tyrick Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace

Position: Forward, Age: 29, Club: Tottenham

Out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi, Richarlison could help Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and himself in one fell swoop.

In the summer, Spurs were looking for £20m for the Brazilian. Now the feeling is they would take a figure below £10m – some sources think £7m may suffice – to move on a player who has been kicking his heels since playing for the Under 21s away to Cheltenham Town in October.

Richarlison saw summer offers from Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama fall through for various reasons and with United desperate to bolster their front line, this one could suit all parties. Richarlison is a strong presser from the front, versatile and better in the air than he is perhaps given credit for. He’s also no stranger to football's dark arts, something Pochettino appreciates.

The 29-year-old would offer a greater goal threat than Joshua Zirkzee, who saw moves of his own collapse in the summer, and showed last season what a threat he can be, scoring 11 league goals.

Spurs just want him out of the building and while that is normally a red flag, United need all the help they can get in a difficult market.

Richarlison is available for a bargain fee in January - even if he comes with some red flags attached

Position: Centre back, Age: 28, Club: AC Milan

United have rarely gone to the continent for recruits in recent seasons. But their limited budget makes Premier League players extremely difficult to acquire.

One option who might be available for a bargain fee is AC Milan's Fikayo Tomori, who is out of contract in the summer. The expectation in Milan is that Tomori will be moved on in January, allowing former United boss Ruben Amorim to add to his defence.

Tomori was initally frozen out by Amorim – he’d have a good ice-breaker should he pitch up at United! – and was even stripped of a squad number, before he was gradually reintroduced.

The England international has started just four games this season – only two in the league – and while Tomori has limitations in the air, he would bring Premier League experience and a level of leadership that is sorely lacking. His ability to bring the ball out and into midfield would make him a regular starter in Manchester.

When Milan won Serie A in 2022, Tomori was aggressive in his press and showed he could play on either side as a centre back, and also slot in at right back when required.

Milan want to sell him, United need defensive reinforcements, and a cut-price deal suits everyone. This one is a no-brainer, thanks to Amorim of all people.

Fikayo Tomori looks set to move on from AC Milan in January with former United boss Ruben Amorim keen to shuffle his defensive pack

Position: Left back/centre back, Age: 29, Club: Stuttgart

An experienced option that could cover multiple positions across the back line, Mittelstadt would prove really shrewd business.

Under contract until 2028, the player has not agitated for a move but sources in Germany have indicated no extension talks are underway at this stage.

Stuttgart are eighth in the Bundesliga and should European football start to look out of reach, a sale of someone like Mittelstadt may become a necessity.

United should look at him even though his resale value would be limited, as he would immediately bring experience and quality. Mittelstadt, who was Germany's first-choice left back at Euro 2024, is a proactive defender that doesn’t shirk challenges and his durability means United could count on him from the off – important given their lack of high-quality options at left back.

Signing Mittelstadt would go against everything the club's executives want to do – but they showed by bringing in the 29-year-old Youri Tielemans in the summer that they are prepared to make exceptions on some older players.

Germany international Maximilian Mittelstadt (right) would add quality at full back

Position: Left back, Age: 23, Club: Real Madrid

Carreras should never have been allowed to leave United, but now comes a chance to rectify the mistake the club made in letting him go two-and-a-half years ago.

The 23-year-old has not been a regular starter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid and a player of his undoubted quality won't be happy with that state of affairs.

Real don’t need to cut their losses on a young player who is contracted through to 2031, which is exactly why Pochettino should go to Mourinho and see if he can take Carreras on loan for the rest of the season.

He is a better creator of chances than Patrick Dorgu or Luke Shaw and while Dorgu offers greater threat in the final third, Carreras feels a more well-rounded option at left back that is a better match-up against the league’s top wingers.

Carreras needs regular starts to develop and here is a chance for Mourinho to do his former side a favour when they are cash-strapped.

United made a mistake in letting Alvaro Carreras (right) go in 2024 - now it is time to rectify it

Folarin Balogun forged a strong connection with Pochettino with the US national team and looks set to leave Monaco in the near future

A striker that looked bound for Everton until a last-minute, deadline-day U-turn in the summer, it is widely known among recruitment staff that Balogun is available in January.

The Arsenal academy graduate has worked under Pochettino extensively with the US national team and, having had a reduced role at Monaco since the botched Everton move, a fresh start under a manager who knows how to get the best out of him would suit everyone.

‘There were just floods (of tears) from many people, but it's bound to happen,’ said Balogun when Pochettino left the USA job. ‘We had a really close relationship, him, his staff and us as players. We were really connected. It was always going to be a sad goodbye for that reason.’

Pochettino and Balogun's desire to reunite will be strong, but money could be an issue here. A loan with a conditional obligation to buy could be the best compromise, with incentives based on United's league position or Balogun's goals scored.

Tottenham Hotspur are stepping up their interest in Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis as Roberto De Zerbi assesses potential attacking reinforcements ahead of the January transfer window.

The 28-year-old Greece international has established himself as one of the most prolific goalscorers in European football, attracting considerable attention from Premier League clubs following his outstanding start to the season.

Tottenham are now closely monitoring his performances, although convincing Benfica to sanction a mid-season departure could prove difficult.

According to Portuguese publication Record, Tottenham have regularly sent scouts to Benfica matches specifically to assess Pavlidis.

The Greek forward has scored an impressive 19 goals in 20 appearances across all competitions this season, further enhancing his reputation as a reliable goalscorer.

Pavlidis has become an important figure in Benfica’s attack, contributing through his movement, physical presence and ability to involve teammates in attacking moves.

However, Tottenham are not alone in their admiration for the striker.

A recent CaughtOffside report revealed that Manchester United are also interested in securing his services.

Benfica’s negotiating position remains strong, with Pavlidis understood to have a €100million release clause in his contract. There is currently no indication that Tottenham have submitted a formal offer.

Signing Pavlidis would represent an interesting departure from Tottenham’s emphasis on recruiting younger players with significant resale potential.

At 28, the Greek international is already in his prime and would arrive with considerable experience rather than requiring several seasons of development.

His intelligent movement inside the penalty area, finishing ability and willingness to contribute outside the box could make him particularly effective in De Zerbi’s attacking system.

However, Tottenham must be careful about the financial commitment involved.

While Pavlidis has consistently delivered goals in Portugal and previously in the Netherlands, adapting to the intensity of Premier League football would present a fresh challenge.

Spending close to his release clause would represent a substantial gamble, particularly given his age.

If Tottenham can negotiate a considerably lower transfer fee, Pavlidis could prove an excellent addition capable of making an immediate impact.

For now, continuing to assess the striker before committing to an expensive January pursuit appears to be the sensible approach.

#1236. Man United FURIOUS with Howard Webb after he backed decision to send off Leny Yoro at Anfield: Club to take fight to Premier League as red card is OVERTURNED after appeal

Published: 10:23 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 02:10 EST, 25 November 2026

Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

But United are furious that Pro Ref boss Webb has refused to admit the error after he backed Barrott’s decision and VAR’s refusal to overturn it on the Mic’d Up show on Sky Sports. The club are determined to take up the matter directly with the Premier League and Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off for pushing Alexander Isak in the back, but United disputed the referee’s view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The FA panel appeared to agree as it rescinded Yoro’s red card and lifted his one-match ban on the basis that he did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity – meaning the Frenchman can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, Webb argued: ‘That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday

‘I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.’

United sources have branded this interpretation as ‘totally wrong’ and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott’s decision.

United dispute that it was subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

Pochettino blamed the decision for United’s defeat at Anfield, and took aim at VAR again after landing in Portugal last night (tues) for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon.

‘I’m very disappointed because I think this kind of thing never can happen,’ said Pochettino, who also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai’s opening goal from the resulting free kick should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola made contact with United’s defensive wall.

‘The referee can make a mistake but if we have VAR what were they doing? We need to take time to review the situation.’

It’s the second time this season that United have been proven to be on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials.

In September, Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand.

Tonight’s (wed) game sees United captain Bruno Fernandes face his old team Sporting amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford after talks over a new contact stalled.

‘We have time to speak about that,’ said Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.’

Asked if he would consider a return to Sporting, who sold him to United for £68million in 2020, Fernandes added: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.’

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Chelsea and Tottenham at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea secured a hard-fought 2-0 away win at Everton last weekend thanks to Pedro Neto’s double, while Tottenham earned their first Premier League victory of the season on Monday, beating Frank Lampard’s Coventry City 3-1 at home.

Arsenal have added Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs to their list of January transfer targets as Mikel Arteta looks to inject more pace and creativity into his attack.

The 22-year-old Portugal international has rebuilt his reputation in Belgium following difficult spells with Ajax and Wolverhampton Wanderers, attracting renewed interest from several Premier League clubs.

However, Arsenal may have to wait until next summer to secure his signature, with Club Brugge reluctant to lose one of their most influential attacking players.

According to Football Insider, Forbs features prominently on Arsenal’s shortlist of left-sided attacking targets ahead of the January transfer window.

However, Club Brugge have already informed the Gunners that the Portuguese winger is not available for a mid-season transfer, particularly with the Belgian club still competing in the Champions League.

Forbs has registered five goals and seven assists across all competitions this season, having contributed to 22 goals during the previous campaign.

The former Manchester City academy player has also impressed at international level, recently scoring Portugal’s winning goal against Wales in the Nations League.

A recent CaughtOffside report revealed that Club Brugge could demand around €30million for Forbs, who remains under contract until 2029. Manchester United and Tottenham have also been monitoring his progress.

Arsenal’s interest in Forbs is understandable, particularly given his explosive acceleration and ability to take on defenders.

Arteta’s side regularly encounter opponents who defend in compact formations, and having another winger capable of beating players individually could help create opportunities in difficult matches.

His versatility across both flanks would also provide valuable rotation and reduce Arsenal’s dependence on Bukayo Saka.

However, his disappointing loan spell at Wolves cannot be completely overlooked. Performing consistently in Belgium and succeeding in the Premier League are two very different challenges.

At around €30million, Forbs could nevertheless represent an attractive alternative to some of Arsenal’s considerably more expensive attacking targets.

The Gunners should avoid paying an inflated January premium simply to overcome Club Brugge’s reluctance to sell.

Continuing to monitor his development before revisiting negotiations next summer would be a sensible approach, particularly if Forbs maintains his impressive performances in European and international football.

Manchester City could face a major battle to retain Erling Haaland next summer, with the Norwegian striker reportedly considering a move away from the Etihad Stadium amid growing uncertainty surrounding the club.

The 26-year-old remains one of the most prolific goalscorers in world football, but City’s disappointing performances and the possibility of significant financial sanctions have fuelled speculation about his long-term future.

Barcelona are emerging as a particularly attractive destination should Haaland decide to pursue a new challenge in 2027.

According to Spanish publication El Nacional, Haaland is seriously considering his future at Manchester City, with Barcelona among his preferred destinations.

City’s recent 2-2 Champions League draw against Napoli highlighted their ongoing struggles, with the English giants managing just one victory in their last five matches across all competitions.

The uncertainty surrounding potential sanctions for City’s financial breaches has further complicated the situation.

Manchester United remain open to selling Marcus Rashford in January despite bringing the England international back into the first-team squad following his loan spell at Barcelona.

The 29-year-old returned to Old Trafford during the summer after the Spanish giants decided against signing him permanently. Although United publicly backed his reintegration, uncertainty continues to surround his long-term future.

With Mauricio Pochettino looking to reshape his squad during the winter transfer window, Rashford could once again find himself facing an uncertain future in Manchester.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, transfer journalist Ben Jacobs revealed that United would still entertain suitable offers for Rashford despite their public stance regarding his return.

The Red Devils are looking to strengthen their defence and attack in January, with the potential arrival of a new forward increasing the possibility of an attacking departure.

Rashford remains contracted to United until 2028, meaning the club are not under immediate pressure to sell him.

However, injuries have disrupted his attempts to re-establish himself at Old Trafford.

According to talkSPORT, Rashford was unavailable for Pochettino’s first match in charge against Liverpool because of a persistent injury initially sustained during the World Cup.

The report also revealed that Barcelona declined to activate their £26million purchase option, instead signing Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United.

United’s willingness to consider offers for Rashford is understandable from a financial perspective, particularly given his substantial wages and the need to strengthen other areas of the squad.

However, selling him in January without giving Pochettino an opportunity to assess him properly could prove premature.

The Argentine’s preference for aggressive, transitional football could suit Rashford’s pace, direct running and ability to exploit space behind opposition defenders.

United are also struggling for attacking consistency, making the departure of an experienced forward potentially counterproductive unless a suitable replacement is secured.

At 29, Rashford still has enough time to rediscover his best form, although he must demonstrate greater consistency and availability.

Pochettino’s arrival offers the academy graduate another opportunity to revive his United career.

If Rashford fails to impress under the new manager, a summer departure could make sense. For now, though, United should prioritise getting him fit and assessing his contribution before making a definitive decision.
