#1207. Worse Than Lammens: Pochettino Must Drop Man Utd Star Youri Tielemans

Manchester United missed the chance to end their six-month wait for an away win as the Reds were held to a 2-2 draw against Sporting CP in the Champions League.

Mauricio Pochettino looked to be on course for a first win as head coach after Bruno Fernandes scored twice to cancel out Luis Suarez's first-half opener. But Senne Lammens gifted Sporting a late equaliser as he failed to deal with a high ball inside the box and dropped it, allowing a thankful Suarez to tap home from close-range.

It was the second of two huge mistakes Lammens made against Sporting. Just minutes after saving a penalty from Suarez, the United goalkeeper came rushing out of his goal and clattered into Maximiliano Araujo, causing referee Szymon Marciniak to point to the spot once again. On this occasion, Suarez made no mistake by burying the ball into the bottom corner.

Although Lammens endured a horror show against Sporting, he wasn't the worst United player on the pitch.

Another 4/10 star let Pochettino down. The man in question is Youri Tielemans, who has struggled since moving to the Reds for £35million from Aston Villa in the summer and had another evening to forget, both in and out of possession at the Jose Avalade Stadium.

Lining up in a two-man defensive midfield alongside Kobbie Mainoo once again, Tielemans was unable to influence the game as much as he would have wanted. Indeed, the 29-year-old completed just 27 successful passes with an 82% passing accuracy.

Just one of his four passes into the final third were accurate, while he made just three progressive passes during his time on the pitch. While Tielemans did make one key pass, United fans are expecting much more from the midfielder, given what he did at Villa and Leicester.

From a defensive point-of-view, Tielemans wasn't much better and won just 50% (6/12) of his duels. He was dribbled past once and committed a team-high four fouls. The Belgian did, however, win four tackles, made one interception, one clearance and two recoveries.

Tielemans' dour night ended in the 93rd minute when he was sent off for two bookable offences. He picked up his first yellow card in the first half before seeing red for a foul on Sergi Altimira.

Due to this, he will now serve a one-match ban for United's next Champions League game, which is a clash at home to Bundesliga side RB Leipzig in December.

Summing it up, Tielemans is nowhere near to the required level needed at United right now and should be dropped ahead of Sunday's huge Premier League game against Brentford.

Mainoo was much more involved against Sporting and should keep his spot in the midfield two alongside £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, who deserves a chance from the off.

Santos is much stronger off the ball than Tielemans and Mainoo, and can help bring a more defensive and solid base alongside a creative midfielder.

On this occasion, Tielemans should drop out of the side due to his form and performance against Sporting, with Mainoo keeping his place and Santos coming in.

Fernandes, who was the hero for United in Lisbon after scoring twice, would therefore retain his place in the attacking midfield role, just in front of Mainoo and Santos.

Tielemans does still have a future at United, but for the time being, Pochettino should take him out of the firing line and give him a rest, allowing Santos a chance to show what he can do.

Man Utd's shocking start to the 2026/27 is record breaking and it has fans worried about relegation, but how many times has that happened in history?

#1206. De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

#1205. Allegri videogame lets you fling Napoli coach’s jacket in fury

Napoli fans can now play a videogame as coach Max Allegri, but rather than figure out tactics or choose line-ups, the main task is to throw his jacket as far as possible.

The former Juventus and Milan boss is famous for launching his jacket at moments of extreme tension on the touchline, and once even tore his tie off while threatening to pull at the shirt too during the Coppa Italia Final victory for Juve.

These Hulk moments are so frequent that they have been turned into a videogame, where you can charge up the arm and fling the clothing all the way out of the stadium and across the Bay of Naples.

If you throw it far enough, legendary Napoli kitman Tommy Starace will bring you some fresh espresso from his Moka.

There is also another level where you can face the demon Adaniel, who looks suspiciously like pundit Daniele Adani, known for having a years-long public feud with Allegri over their fundamentally different views of attacking football.

A post shared by Spazio Napoli (@spazionapoli.it)

ALLEGRI, ONE THE THE FEW REMAINING STONE AGE ERA COACHES!

^ Darn, just grow up. The man has won more Scudetti than 98% of the coaches in Serie A today (6). The narrative around “stone age” is so tiring.

@Rossomilan: He inherited a stellar squad of BBBC with a never-die attitude from Conte.

Even Spalletti has won a Scudetto, but he’s a horrible dinosaur now, and it’s only because of Juventus’ incompetence that he’s the head coach.

Propaganda or fact? Or are you and most other commenters on Football Italia sheeples who can’t critically analyse for yourself? Yet if it was Zdenek Zeman – with his attack first defend later attitude you’d be criticising him too for losing too much. Different football philosophies for different times. You can win 1-0 or 5-4. I know which I prefer. If you don’t like Allegri’s football – fine – get over it and move on.

Everyone calling for Ancelotti’s head in the Brazil NT, yet one of the greatest to have managed (Guardiola) is one of very few to have commented on the substance of him as a manager. Grow up with your “stellar” Bianconeri propaganda. Comment section on this site full of it sometimes.

#1204. Alongside Calvert-Lewin: Leeds Have Just Made Another Clever Decision

Leeds United have triggered a club option to extend Lukas Nmecha's contract at Elland Road.

Nmecha, 27, joined the Whites on a free transfer in June 2025, following his departure from Wolfsburg. He penned a two-year deal in West Yorkshire and scored on his debut in a 1-0 win against Everton.

But the German had to wait three months to find the net again, when he struck in a 3-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest. That started a mini purple patch for Nmecha, who netted in three successive matches and became Daniel Farke's first-choice striker, replacing Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

However, that is as good as it has got for Nmecha in a Leeds shirt. After suffering a hamstring injury, he lost his place in the starting line-up back to Calvert-Lewin and the ex-Everton man hasn't looked back since, cementing himself as Farke's main man up front.

GIVEMESPORT exclusively revealed on Tuesday that Calvert-Lewin was set to sign a new contract himself, as he becomes the Yorkshire outfit's talisman.

It has left Nmecha as back-up, and with Calvert-Lewin starting all 11 Premier League matches this season, he has had to make do with appearances on the left and in the No.10.

Indeed, Nmecha started the 1-0 win against Tottenham earlier this month as one of the two attacking midfielders alongside Sean Longstaff. But after struggling, he dropped down to the bench for the trip to Chelsea on Saturday, a game the Whites ended up winning 4-1.

Noah Okafor, who replaced Nmecha in the XI, scored twice as Leeds moved up to seventh in the Premier League table and fans are now believing a European push could be on.

Despite the fact Nmecha is not in Farke's best starting side, Leeds do not want to lose him. And now, according to The Athletic, the final formalities are being concluded on a one-year contract extension for Nmecha after the Whites triggered an option in his current deal.

Nmecha was due to be out of contract at the end of the season, but he will be tied down until 2028 once the paperwork is finalised, ensuring he is still at Leeds for at least another 18 months.

While some Leeds fans are a little frustrated that the club have triggered the extension on Nmecha's contract, given the fact he hasn't scored since February and has struggled this season, he is still an important squad player and will be a cost-effective option if the Whites secure European football.

Leeds will need a bigger squad if they reach Europe, and given Nmecha's experience on the continent in Belgium and Germany, he could be crucial for Farke in that competition.

As well as that, he is one of the lowest earners in the first-team squad at £45,000 per-week and there isn't too many better players Leeds can replace him with who would take that wage and join on a free transfer. For me, it's a no-brainer to extend Nmecha's contract.

Alongside the fact he could be important for Leeds if they secure European football, the extension to Nmecha's deal also protects his value and means the Whites could sell him to make profit.

And should Leeds fail to make Europe, that is the option they should take. Selling Nmecha in those circumstances would make sense, as it's clear he is not good enough for a regular spot in the Premier League XI but can cut it in the Europa League or Conference League, for sure.

Nmecha can still make an impact from the bench and even in the FA Cup for Leeds this season. He set up Calvert-Lewin's equaliser in the draw against Brentford in August and has shown that he can influence matches when needed, even if he isn't as effective as the likes of Okafor.

Daniel Farke's side ran riot for their first Premier League victory at Stamford Bridge in decades

#1203. Erling Haaland sparks fear among fans after concerning TV interview as he admits he is 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli

Published: 04:06 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 08:33 EST, 25 November 2026

Manchester City fans have expressed concern over Erling Haaland's despondent interview following their Champions League draw with Napoli, with the star admitting he is 'questioning everything' amid their slump in form.

Enzo Maresca's side rescued a late draw at the Etihad on Tuesday night, with Rayan Cherki equalising in the 86th minute to secure a 2-2 draw with Napoli.

The result, however, continued an underwhelming run of form with Man City having won just twice in their last seven matches – one of which was achieved in a penalty shoot-out against Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

Man City have suffered defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League in the run, as well as drawing with Fulham on the weekend.

Haaland, who captained Man City against Napoli, admitted post-match to TNT Sports that their underwhelming form has left the squad questioning themselves.

'We were not able to control and attack the game in the way we want,' Haaland said. 'Football is easy and difficult. When you win it's easy and you know what to do. When you don't you start questioning everything.

Erling Haaland cut a despondent figure as he admitted to 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli continued their underwhelming form

🗣️ "I have no idea what we were missing. You could feel it in the last few games that there's something that's not clicking fully."@Erling reflects on @ManCity's 2-2 draw with Napoli.🎤 @AndyKerrtv #UCL | #ManCity pic.twitter.com/Cx2Hzieom3

'The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy.

'We have so much quality so it's about getting the quality out in every player. We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best.'

Haaland admitted in another interview with Bein Sports that the run of form 'hurts', with the star having offered a resigned laugh when asked whether the draw against Napoli should be considered a 'good point'.

The 26-year-old was seen looking down throughout the minute and a half interview, while he also rubbed his face with his hand as he looked to find answers for Man City's recent struggles.

'How the game was we managed to come back two times, but we demand more,' Haaland said.

'We have to do better and find some ways to control the game more and perform in a better way.

'I have no idea what we were missing. You could feel it in the last few games that it is not clicking fully and we have to find out, stay positive and get the best out of every single day.

'With and without the armband I feel huge responsibility because all I want to do is perform for this club and win games for Man City and right now we are not doing that. It hurts.'

Fans quickly noted Haaland's downbeat responses to questions and despondent body language during the interview.

Man City fans have expressed concerns over Haaland's downbeat responses and body language in the interview

Fans claimed they have never seen Haaland 'looking this flat' and suggested the star 'looks distraught' amid their underwhelming run

'I've never seen Haaland looking this flat. Not even close to it,' one commented.

'At least he’s being honest with himself. Looks distraught,' a second said, with a third writing 'Extremely concerning.'

'Never seen Erling Haaland look like this before,' another added, while a Man City fan wrote 'You can really tell how confused Haaland is from his expression. They don’t have confidence in their own football.'

One went as far as claiming 'Haaland looks like he’s done with Manchester City…' while sharing footage of his reaction to one of Napoli's goals on the night.

Other fans questioned whether Haaland and his Man City team-mates' recent slump may be related to concerns over the potential punishment the club could face for breaching financial rules.

Man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Man City face Arsenal in a crucial match on Sunday as they look to make inroads in the Gunners six point lead at the top of the Premier League

Haaland had pushed back against suggestions the case had affected their form during the international break, while stressing he was committed long-term to the club.

The forward's first answer to Norwegian broadcaster TV2 had spanned two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges after he was asked about the club's situation.

'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland said.

'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle…

'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'

He continued: 'It's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

The Man City star, who signed a nine-and-a-half-year contract in late 2024, told Norwegian television earlier this month that his focus was on helping the team to turn their form around.

The draw against Napoli leaves Man City lying sixth in the Champions League table - which would be enough to see Maresca's side to qualify for the last-16.

Man City face a crucial clash on the weekend when they face reigning champions Arsenal in the Premier League, as they look to halve the six-point gap to the leaders at the top of the table.

#1202. Forget Fernandes: Man Utd Manager Pochettino Now Has Unexpected Undroppable Star

Mauricio Pochettino was denied his first win as Manchester United head coach after Senne Lammens' late blunder ensured the Reds were held to a 2-2 draw against Sporting CP in the Champions League.

United looked to be on course to end their six-month wait for an away victory after Bruno Fernandes scored twice to cancel out Luis Suarez's first-half spot-kick. But Lammens spilled the ball in the box for Suarez to equalise for his second of the game as United had to settle for a point at the Jose Avalade Stadium.

Pochettino will be frustrated that United didn't hold on after Fernandes sparked an inspiring second-half comeback. Suarez had given Sporting the lead from the penalty spot, but the Reds responded just after half-time, scoring twice in three minutes.

First, Fernandes equalised from the spot after Lisandro Martinez had been brought down. Then the Portuguese completed his brace with a bizarre goal, which came thanks to the ball rebounding off a divot in the ground and looping over the goalkeeper.

But Lammens gifted Sporting a route back into the game as he failed to deal with a routine ball into the box and flapped it into the path of Suarez, who made no mistake from close-range.

It meant that United's winless away win stretches to nine games and ensures Pochettino will have to wait to record his first victory with Brentford next up in the Premier League this weekend.

Although Fernandes scored twice and was the standout player on the pitch, there were a couple of other United players who impressed. One of those was Leny Yoro, who impressed at the back and has to be a nailed-on starter for Pochettino going forward. The Frenchman proved against Sporting that he is United's best defender and deserves to be playing week-in week-out.

Starting in a new-look back-four alongside Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Noussair Mazraoui, Yoro didn't put much of a foot wrong. Indeed, he shone in a defence that looked more settled and forced Sporting to have just ONE big chance from open play. That even came from the Lammens mistake which led to Suarez's second goal, nothing Yoro or the rest of the back-four could have done.

Looking at Yoro's individual performance, he was solid from a defensive point-of-view. He made eight defensive actions, five ball recoveries, won five out of six ground duels and won two out of three aerial duels.

As well as that, Yoro was excellent in possession and looked comfortable on the ball. He completed 55 out of 57 of his passes, created one chance, made seven line-breaking passes, and made three long passes.

It is the most consistent Yoro has looked this season, without a doubt, and there is an argument to be made that it was the best he has been since he signed for United from Lille two-and-a-half years ago.

Some United fans compared Yoro's performance to how Raphael Varane was during his prime at Old Trafford, and there is a case that he could become as good as him in the future, should he perform like that more often.

Yoro was assured when defending, made some important tackles and kept the in-form Suarez for most of the game, even if he did score twice, albeit one was from the spot and the other came from Lammens' error.

Now that his one-match ban has been lifted, Yoro should be on Pochettino's teamsheet for the home game against Brentford on Sunday. He should be kept in the XI after impressing at Sporting and should be a regular in the XI long-term.

Other than Fernandes and Yoro, the other nine United players who started against Sporting should be worried about keeping their place in the XI. Yoro has the right to be considered as undroppable right now, he was excellent for the Reds.

It's a remarkable turnaround for Yoro, who was sent off against Liverpool on Sunday and looked devoid of confidence. But 72 hours later, he performed the opposite and that should now be the minimum he produces in a United shirt moving forward.

#1201. Montella: ‘Turkiye ambition, Milan chaos, Roma success and my apology to Capello’

Former Turkiye manager Vincenzo Montella looks back over his career, including the ‘chaos’ at Milan and ‘never believing’ in Cristiano Ronaldo, plus why he ‘must apologise’ to Fabio Capello.

The Little Aeroplane is now a free agent after he was dismissed by the Turkiye squad for losing all their Nations League games, despite taking them into the Nations League A and qualifying for the 2026 World Cup.

“When I arrived, they were afraid that they wouldn’t qualify for the European Championships, but we did it, and then got into the World Cup and the Nations League A,” Montella told La Gazzetta dello Sport.

“Naturally, the end to this experience hurt, but at times unpredictable things can happen in football.”

His playing career was most closely associated with Roma, and it is also where he made his senior debut as a coach.

“Making my debut on the Roma bench at the age of 36 was special. I already enjoyed reading the game from the touchline, especially when I started to spend a lot of time on the bench as a player, but when you become a coach, it opens up a whole new world.”

Montella’s first major job was at Silvio Berlscuoni’s Milan in 2016, but there were more downs than ups.

“It was always my dream, because I supported Milan when I was a kid, seeing Marco van Basten. Berlusconi was a gentleman, even if he often got involved and tried to push me towards certain decisions. He was accustomed to a squad full of Ballon d’Or winners, but we didn’t have them. I joked that if he bought me one, I could play more attacking football too.

“That club had more publicity slogans than concrete messages. There was a lot of chaos in the second year, a change of ownership, many new players, and just a general chaos in the transfer strategy. We didn’t always share ideas, sometimes I wasn’t even consulted.

“I think when the time came to sign a striker, I was told the budget was all used up.”

There had been talk that summer about Cristiano Ronaldo coming to Milan, before his experience at Juventus.

“I never believed in that, it seemed more like Fantasy Football,” insisted Montella.

When it comes to another of his former clubs, he has high hopes for Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma, especially with Donyell Malen scoring four goals in a single game.

“I scored four in the derby, though, marked by Alessandro Nesta, so it’s a bit different,” smiled the former striker about his record in 2002.

“I do think Malen will be the Capocannoniere this season, if he keeps going like this, he can get 30 or more. Roma can challenge for the Scudetto to the end, then who knows?”

Roma have not won the Scudetto since 2001, when Capello was the coach and Montella the striker along with Francesco Totti and Gabriel Batistuta.

“We had a big party at my house the day after the final game. Capello was not invited, but he turned up anyway. If I had opened the door, I’d have made him run around the building a couple of times first,” revealed Montella.

“I do think I owe Capello an apology, at times I didn’t behave professionally, and I regret that.”

#1200. Iraola Must Be Tearing His Hair Out With Liverpool Star, He's Not The Same Player

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola must be tearing his hair out with what he's seeing from Milos Kerkez since his arrival.

Iraola previously managed Kerkez at Bournemouth, and he enjoyed a phenomenal spell with the Cherries under his management.

The Hungarian international was a flying full-back who loved to try to make things happen in the final third, and that's why Liverpool made a move to secure his signature.

Many Liverpool supporters must have been hoping that Kerkez would flourish under Iraola, given they've previously worked together.

Unfortunately, that simply hasn't been the case, and Iraola must be confused as to what's happened to him.

Against Club Brugge, Kerkez started on the left-hand side of defence. It was far from a disastrous performance from the Hungarian, who was incredibly solid defensively, but he's still showing a major weakness.

Kerkez simply isn't the same player he once was when it comes to how he contributes in the final third.

The 23-year-old struggles to look after the ball in possession, particularly when he ventures into the opposition half.

Kerkez completed just 78% of his passes against Club Brugge, while he also fluffed a shot from inside the penalty area.

This isn't an isolated situation for Kerkez, as he's yet to produce a goal or an assist for Liverpool so far this season.

Last term, despite playing 48 games, Kerkez contributed with just four goal contributions for Liverpool.

Although Kerkez's hasn't ever been a phenomenal contributor in the final third, it's just his overall game that appears to be lacking in attack.

Iraola will undoubtedly be happy with what he's seeing from him defensively, but he needs to see more from him going forward.

In modern football, full-backs who can contribute in both halves are incredibly important, especially when Liverpool usually have a defensive option on the other side in Ronald Araujo. It's not hampering Liverpool too much at the moment, considering their recent form, but they still remain seven points behind Arsenal in the Premier League table.

Rio Ngumoha has impressed for Liverpool under Andoni Iraola, but there is another Reds star that is going under the radar

Liverpool fans are so used to having a left-back in Andy Robertson, who contributed so significantly in the final third throughout his career.

In his prime, Robertson hit 15 assists in one season while regularly reaching double figures for assists while with Liverpool.

That could be the main frustration from Liverpool supporters who are still unsure whether Kerkez is the right man for them.

They will likely be regularly comparing him to someone like Robertson, especially when they're also used to Trent Alexander-Arnold on the opposite side, one of the most creative defenders in world football.

Iraola must be tearing his hair out at why Kerkez just doesn't seem to be the same player when it comes to how he acts in the final third.

#1199. Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner

“Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane said as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him.

In truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he said of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.”

Kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he said. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.”

So much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success.

Kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and said: “You held it together. You got through it.” It showed how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied: “Yes”.

What a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany.

Kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best.

Kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. Those numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world class and legendary.

Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg

For his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago – he took 129 matches.

Kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals.

Both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he said. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do.

Those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his two goals against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup that saved his team and Thomas Tuchel from an embarrassing early exit.

The Prince of Wales, who has been FA president since 2006, congratulated Kane on “a fantastic achievement”.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments,” Prince William wrote on Instagram.

Kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example on and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season.

And he works hard, so very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s.

That work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and said he could be top-scorer – but he proved them wrong.

They probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. Wow, what a night.

There was a secretive photo shoot at the training ground and then I picked up the award before a game against Derby County. It has changed a bit since. It probably means more to me now than it did then.

“My heart is with Harry Kane. I would like a new English partner. Sadly we lost Kevin Keegan, who was the only other living English winner. But you could make a case for a lot of people. It is very open this year. Kylian Mbappe has not won any trophies, but top scorer in La Liga, CL, WC and it is an individual award. You cannot complain if somebody like that won the award. Every time I watch Lamine Yamal play, literally, I nearly fall off the sofa in awe of him. He is just so good isn’t he. Kane has had an amazing year, too, personally. I think it is between those three.”

By Christian FalkGermany do not have a single player among the 30 in the running to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night – but Bayern Munich do have England captain Harry Kane.

For the 35-time German champions, the award is perhaps even more important than it is for the peerless striker himself. The Bayern hierarchy are planning to travel to the Palladium Theatre en masse to support Kane.

Kane is not only Bayern’s top striker, he is their international figurehead and, internally, their poster-boy professional. Club patron and honorary president Uli Hoeness described the England captain as the best signing in the club’s history. Hoeness even went so far as to say he loves Kane, and he is not alone in this.

There's only one Harry Kane. https://t.co/NfZEFmjaUN

Hoeness is one of many in the club’s leadership who have been endlessly promoting Kane to help the 33-year-old fulfil his lifelong dream of winning the trophy. Bayern officials have been campaigning on his behalf for weeks.

First up was manager Vincent Kompany, who remains in hospital for tests after collapsing at Bayern’s training ground on Friday. Kompany said: “If he can now crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be fitting given the way he plays for the team.”

The plaudits kept coming. Whether it was sporting director Max Eberl (“He has more than earned the Ballon d’Or. Anyone who loves football loves characters like Harry Kane”), chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen (“One thing is clear – anyone talking about this year’s greatest individual honours cannot overlook Harry Kane”) or president Herbert Hainer (“Harry Kane embodies the idea that sporting greatness is incomplete without greatness of character. He would be a worthy World Footballer of the Year”), everyone at the club is fighting for Kane.

The official Ballon d’Or website has announced Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners of the main prize in an embarrassing blunder for the organisation.

Three separate articles were published before quickly being taken down.

The headline on Kane’s article read: ‘Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season’.

The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

The choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

In total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

#1198. Champions League official line-ups: Inter vs. VfB Stuttgart

Inter rely on Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram again, with Djed Spence and Carlos Augusto on the wings in a must-win match against impressive VfB Stuttgart.

It kicks off at San Siro at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and PSG-Roma on the Champions League Liveblog.

The Nerazzurri were shaken at the weekend by fumbling a two-goal advantage to be held 4-4 by Atalanta in Serie A.

They had started the season losing both Champions League fixtures to Real Madrid and Club Brugge, but got back on track winning the next two against Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord.

Hakan Calhanoglu suffered a thigh strain in Bergamo and is out for at least a month, along with Ange-Yoan Bonny, while Lautaro Martinez is not yet ready to be risked from the start after returning from a month out with a similar problem.

That means Pio Esposito hopes to continue his fine form after a hat-trick against Atalanta, partnered by Marcus Thuram.

Henrikh Mkhitaryan and Petar Sucic are chosen to step into midfield, while Manuel Akanji returns in defence.

Carlos Augusto is also preferred to Federico Dimarco on the left flank.

VfB Stuttgart are ahead of Inter in the Champions League table coming in, as they beat Viking and Slovan Bratislava, drew 1-1 with Atletico Madrid, then lost 2-0 away to Galatasaray.

Angelo Stiller, Leo Sauer and Luca Jaquez are back in the squad despite carrying knocks, while Dan-Axel Zagadou, Stefan Drljaca, Justin Diehl and Leonidas Stergiou are not on the UEFA list.

Jamie Leweling was targeted by several Serie A clubs over the summer, providing pace and unpredictability with Bilal El Khannouss, but Leweling is surprisingly benched along with Deniz Undav.

Inter: J Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Sucic, Mkhitaryan, Carlos Augusto; P Esposito, M Thuram

Stuttgart: Seimen; Jeltsch, Chabot, Hendriks; Vagnoman, Nartey, Spalt, Mittelstäd; El Khannouss, Demirovic, Führich

#1197. Ex-England defender Conor Coady emerges as managerial candidate for League One side Blackpool just two weeks after retiring

Published: 09:12 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 09:12 EST, 25 November 2026

Conor Coady has emerged as one of the candidates to become new head coach at Blackpool.

The struggling League One side are looking for a new manager after firing Ian Evatt on his birthday last week.

They salvaged a draw against Leicester City on Tuesday to stay just above the drop zone in 20th place with caretaker Steve Thompson in charge.

The Tangerines are understood to have been inundated with applications with the likes of Conor Hourihane, who left Leicester City as assistant manager earlier this month, Matt Bloomfield, formerly Oxford United boss, and Richie Wellens of Leyton Orient among the leading names in the frame.

However, Daily Mail Sport understands former England, Wolves and Everton defender Coady is also being considered.

Conor Coady, pictured here working as England Under-21s assistant, could take over at Blackpool

The 33-year-old retired from playing on November 6 after stints with Wrexham and Charlton Athletic and took up a role as assistant to Lee Carsley in the England U21 set-up in September, replacing Ashley Cole.

Coady had also been helping out within his first club Liverpool's U21 set-up, prior to his deadline day departure from Wrexham.

He is keen to make the step up in club coaching and was linked with a role at Barnsley in recent weeks.

#1196. Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 659, pages 979–986 (2026) Cite this article

Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics.

T.P. took the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy measurements. H.S. analysed the transport data with input from A.S., S.K., D.G.-G., B.Y. and E.P. H.S. wrote the paper, with major edits from E.P., and input from A.S., S.X.W., H.B., D.G.-G. and B.Y. All authors discussed the results and commented on the paper.

a, High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) image of the NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbon with Nb (3.4 nm) seed layer. The electrically-conducting width of this device is ~12.5 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed, together with their corresponding Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), obtained from the boxed regions in panel a. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions. In total, three NbP (1.5 nm) nanoribbons were examined by cross-sectional STEM. Across these samples, we observe consistent structural and compositional characteristics, including similar NbP crystallinity and sidewall oxidation, which support the scaling behaviour reported in this work. Additional STEM characterization was not performed on thicker NbP nanoribbons, as the thinnest nanoribbons are most relevant to the main conclusions of this study.

a, HAADF image of the NbP (1.5 nm)/Nb (3.4 nm) nanoribbon with an electrically-conducting width of ~18 nm. b, Magnified view of the nanocrystalline NbP layer and crystalline Nb seed layer, together with their corresponding FFT, obtained from the boxed regions. c,d, Bright-field image (c) and EDS elemental map (d) of the same device, showing distinct material compositions of each region. e, EELS linescan profiles of Nb (blue) and P (red) normalized intensity as a function of position along the direction indicated in panel c. f-h, Representative nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data at probe positions within the sapphire substrate (f), Nb layer (g), and NbP layer (h), with indexed reflections confirming the distinct crystal structure of each region. i-k, Orientation template matching of the representative NBED pattern in f–h, for the sapphire substrate (i), Nb layer (j) and NbP layer (k). Coloured symbols indicate the local crystallographic orientation of the best-matching template for that pattern. l-n, Phase template matching of the same patterns for the sapphire substrate (l), Nb layer (m) and NbP layer (n).

a, Schematic of the scaling mechanism for conventional metals, with surface scattering and grain boundary scattering. b, As thickness and width of NbP are reduced, the conduction is consistent with the growing dominance of surface carriers, which are disorder-tolerant, with reduced scattering. The total sheet conductance in this case is a sum of the sheet conductance contributed from bulk carriers and surface carriers. c, For thick NbP, bulk carriers dominate the transport, and thus conventional scaling laws apply, with pronounced surface and grain boundary scattering. d, The Fuchs-Sondheimer (FS) and Mayadas-Shatzkes (MS) model fitting of 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, showing an excellent fit. The extracted resistivity with increasing width (W → ∞) is 56.3 μΩ∙cm, which matches the literature results. e, Sheet conductance (GNbP,□) of 1.5 nm NbP as a function of width (red curve), extracted from Fig. 2d of the main text. The sheet conductance from bulk carriers (extracted from Hall measurement) follows the conventional FS-MS scaling model (black dashed line), where the sheet conductance from surface carriers increases as the width decreases due to the increased surface area/volume ratio, as indicated by the purple dashed line. At this ultrathin thickness (1.5 nm), bulk carriers experience strong scattering, resulting in very small bulk carrier sheet conductance. f, GNbP,□ of 10 nm NbP as a function of width (blue curve). At NbP thickness of 10 nm, 3D bulk carriers and 2D top and bottom surface carriers contribute comparably to transport, as shown in Fig. 4b. At this thickness, as the nanoribbon width is reduced, the enhancement in surface conduction is insufficient to offset the increased scattering of bulk carriers. Consequently, bulk transport dominates in this regime, leading to a net reduction of sheet conductance (i.e., increased resistivity) with decreasing width, more similar to conventional metal wires. We note that there could be subtle differences in sidewall roughness and damage in the thicker nanoribbons compared to the thinner ones. See Supplementary Note 2 for the modelling details and more discussion.

a, Bulk Brillouin-zone schematic showing the two mirror planes and nodal rings from the band inversion. b, Representative band dispersion along Γ-S-M’, where the curves calculated without spin-orbit coupling (SOC) show the nodal-ring-related band inversion (plotted in green), and the curves calculated with SOC show the corresponding gap opening (black dashed lines). c, Real-space crystal view highlighting the helical states along the projected mirror line on the surface. d, Surface-state spectrum along \(\overline{\Gamma }\)-\(\overline{{\rm{X}}}\)-\(\overline{\Gamma }\)’, where the narrow Weyl-point window (grey shadow) hosts three pairs of helical states (indicated by arrows) that form the main part of the Fermi arcs, while remnant spin-split surface branches remain visible over a broader energy window (broad green shadow). Blue and red colours indicate the ‘± Sy’ spin polarization at opposite momenta, showing the helical feature. In summary, the narrow Fermi-arc structure is embedded inside a much broader nodal-ring-derived surface-state sector set by the band inversion. See Supplementary Note 7 for more discussion on bulk-topology hierarchy and topological surface-state interpretation.

a, Slab model along the [001] direction for the surface state calculations. Here, the 2 × 2 × 3 supercell is shown as an example. A 4.5 nm thick slab structure of the 1 × 1 × 4 supercell was used in the calculations. b,c, Surface band structures with Nb (b) and P (c) terminations along high-symmetry lines. Blue and red bands indicate the surface states of the Nb and P terminations, respectively. Bulk-projected states shown in pale blue are depicted as the background. The charge neutral point is set to 0 eV. d-f, Surface-projected Fermi surfaces with Nb (upper panels) and P (lower panels) terminations at 0 eV (d), −0.2 eV (e), and −0.4 eV (f). Darker colours represent larger contributions projected from the surface. Weyl points projected on the 2D Brillouin zone are shown as green and purple dots for opposite chirality. The constant energy cuts show surface-dominant open contours over a broad energy window, indicating that Weyl-derived surface bands persist even when the chemical potential is shifted deep into the hole-doped regime, which implies the robustness of the topological surface character. In addition, for the 4.5 nm thick NbP film, the top and bottom surface states exhibit minimal hybridization, except near the Weyl point projections where they meet each other. The Fermi-arc states remain largely unhybridized because they are well separated in momentum space. Even at momenta where they intersect, the resulting hybridization gap is negligible. See Supplementary Note 8 for the modelling details and more discussion.

a, Slab model from the NbP (001) film with thickness d = 1.5 nm and width W = 4.4 to 5.7 nm. b, The one-dimensional (1D) band structure of a W = 5 nm nanoribbon along ky direction. The edge projection is highlighted in purple to show the edge states, while the bulk states are shown in pale blue. Near EF, the edge-projected subbands form an electron-like pocket, consistent with the negative pedge values (panel f). c-e, The spin projection to Sx (c), Sy (d), and Sz (e) components, respectively, for the edge state. The blue and red represent opposite signs of spin polarization. These edge states exhibit a pronounced spin texture arising from strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in noncentrosymmetric NbP where Sx and Sz components are locked to the ky momentum in a Rashba-type SOC. This reduces the wavefunction overlap between counter-propagating modes, thereby suppressing the leading backscattering channel, which indicates high-mobility edge conduction. f, The carrier densities from edge (pedge) and 2D film (p2D) are extracted from linear fitting of the total ribbon density (p1D) by p1D = pedge + p2DW, at varying W. Wc denotes the cross-over width at which the edge carrier density would dominate the transport over the top and bottom surface carrier density. Here, Wc ≈ 0 indicates that the enhanced edge conduction of ultrathin films is not primarily driven by an increased edge carrier density. Instead, it is more plausibly attributed to an enhanced carrier mobility arising from reduced backscattering as the edge dimension approaches the quasi-1D limit. See more details in Supplementary Notes 2 and 8. g, Agreement between the nanoribbon fitting (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{NR}}}\)) and that obtained from independent slab film calculations (\({p}_{2{\rm{D}}}^{{\rm{slab}}}\)) which corresponds to the d = 1.5 nm thickness in Supplementary Fig. 10. This agreement supports the self-consistency of our calculations across both the nanoribbon and thin-film geometries.

a, Temperature-dependent effective resistivity (ρeff) of NbP films with different thicknesses up to 90 nm, measured from Hall bar devices. These films have a 3.4 nm Nb seed layer, whose resistivity is measured separately (black symbols). b, Low-temperature limit (2-10 K) of panel a. The smallest superconducting transition temperature Tc (~2.2 K) is in the 3.4 nm Nb layer (black symbols), while higher Tc are observed in the NbP/Nb films, and Tc decreases monotonically with thicker NbP. The symbol colours follow the convention in panel a. c,d, Temperature-dependent sheet conductance (GNbP,□) (c) and resistivity (ρNbP) (d) for all NbP thicknesses, after subtracting the Nb seed contribution. e, ρNbP as a function of NbP thickness at 300 K and 10 K. For comparison, the ρNbP values of nanoribbons with the widest widths (Fig. 2d of the main text) are slightly higher than those from Hall measurements at 300 K, possibly due to process-induced damage during nanofabrication. f, Temperature-dependent ρeff of a ~5 nm-thick Nb control film, measured from a Hall bar device. The residual resistivity ratio (RRR) is 1.48, and the Tc is ~4.2 K. Inset: enlarged view of the low-temperature region. The presence of NbP appears to promote superconductivity in NbP/Nb films. The superconducting proximity effect is one plausible interpretation, although changes in disorder and enhanced inter-grain coupling (in the presence of NbP layer) could also contribute. We also cannot fully rule out the formation of an interfacial superconducting layer at the NbP/Nb interface. The NbP sheet conductance is obtained by subtracting the sheet conductance of the Nb layer (measured independently on control Nb films) from the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack. The extracted NbP resistivity is then obtained by dividing the NbP thickness by the NbP sheet conductance, i.e. ρNbP = dNbP/GNbP,□, where GNbP,□ = Gtot,□ - GNb,□ and Gtot,□ = dtot/ρeff, where Gtot,□ is the total sheet conductance of the NbP/Nb stack, dtot is the total stack thickness and ρeff is the measured effective resistivity (panel a). The GNbP,□ (panel c) represents the NbP sheet conductance after subtracting the independently-measured Nb seed contribution. Additional validation of the subtraction method using Pt/Nb stacks is provided in Supplementary Fig. 19. Control experiments using Pt/Nb stacks validate that the subtraction procedure itself does not generate an anomalous resistivity trend. Nevertheless, the conductance of the Nb seed layer within NbP/Nb stacks cannot be independently measured and it cannot be said, with absolute certainty, that its behaviour is identical to that of the separately measured Nb control film. Thus, the extracted NbP resistivity relies, by necessity, on the model used.

a-c, Hall resistance (Rxy) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for 3.4 nm Nb (a), 1.5 nm NbP (b), and 10 nm NbP (c). For the NbP films (b,c), the Nb seed layer contribution is subtracted at each corresponding temperature to extract NbP Hall response, using the same two-layer Hall conduction model described in the supplement. d, Effective three-dimensional carrier density (p3D) for all films, revealing opposite temperature-dependence: ultrathin 1.5 nm NbP shows an increasing p3D upon cooling, whereas both thicker NbP (10 nm) and Nb (3.4 nm) display decreasing p3D. (This figure is also included in the main text as Fig. 4d and is reproduced here for convenience). e, Effective hole mobility (μp) of the same films vs. temperature. NbP films exhibit a pronounced increase in mobility upon cooling due to suppressed phonon scattering, whereas the 3.4 nm Nb film shows only a slight rise in mobility, indicating that its transport remains strongly limited by surface scattering.

a-c, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at various temperatures for films of Nb seed layer (3.4 nm) (a), for NbP (1.5 nm) on the Nb seed (b), and for NbP (10 nm) on the Nb seed (c). All measurements were performed with the magnetic field applied perpendicular to the film plane and current direction. At low temperatures, all films exhibit a pronounced negative cusp near low field regions, arising from the interplay of superconducting fluctuations and weak antilocalization. d-e, Longitudinal sheet resistance (Rxx) vs. magnetic field (B) measured at 1.8 K for both 1.5 nm thick NbP (on 3.4 nm Nb seed layer) and for the Nb layer (3.4 nm) evaluated separately. Measurements were performed with B field perpendicular to the film plane and current direction (d), and with B applied in-plane (e). The superconducting transition temperatures are Tc ~ 6 K for the 1.5 nm NbP (on Nb) and ~2.2 K for the 3.4 nm Nb film (see Fig. 3d of the main text). The upper critical field Hc2, defined as the midpoint between the normal state resistance and zero resistance, is extracted. At 1.8 K, the out-of-plane critical field \({H}_{c2}^{\perp }\) is 2.2 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and 0.38 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The in-plane critical field at 1.8 K exceeds 9 T for NbP (1.5 nm) and reaches 4.44 T for Nb (3.4 nm). The superconducting coherence length estimates are provided in the supplement. The sense current used for Hall bar measurements is 0.5 mA, corresponding to a current density of ~0.1 MA/cm2 for the NbP (1.5 nm) film and ~0.15 MA/cm2 for the 3.4 nm Nb control, with the same 100 μm Hall bar device width. We note that this sense current is well below the superconducting critical current: even when we increased the sense current up to 10 mA, we were unable to suppress the superconducting state at 1.8 K.

a, Cross-sectional HAADF STEM image of the alternating NbP/Nb multilayers grown on sapphire. b-d, Denoised nanobeam electron diffraction (NBED) patterns extracted from 4D-STEM data for all Nb layers (Nb layers 1-3) showing consistent body-centred cubic (bcc) diffraction symmetry with indexed reflections, confirming crystalline quality across all Nb layers. Scale bars: 0.5 Å−1. e, EDS line scan across the multilayer stack showing Nb (blue), P (red), and Al (light brown) as a function of position, integrated over a ~ 5nm wide region along the direction indicated by the yellow arrow in panel a, confirming periodic composition and abrupt elemental transitions at each NbP/Nb interface. f-h, denoised NBED patterns from NbP layers 1–3, displaying diffraction symmetry consistent with the NbP crystal structure with indexed reflections, consistent with uniform phase and crystallographic orientation throughout the multilayer stack. The diffraction spots become progressively broader from layer 1 to layer 3, suggesting a gradual decrease in crystalline coherence in NbP layers further from the substrate. This is further supported by the emergence of diffuse ring features in the Layer 3 diffraction pattern, indicative of increasing structural disorder.

#1195. Champions League official line-ups: PSG vs. Roma

Roma aim for the stars with Santiago Castro, Matias Soulé and Manu Koné against giants Paris Saint-Germain, as Paulo Dybala, Bryan Cristante and top scorer Donyell Malen are benched.

It kicks off at the Parc des Princes at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Inter vs. Stuttgart on the Champions League liveblog.

It has been a tricky campaign for the Giallorossi so far, as they are pushing for the top of the Serie A table and still unbeaten there, but have highlighted a distinct lack of experience in Europe.

This saw them twice throw away two-goal leads to Real Madrid and Manchester United, leaving them on four points in as many rounds.

The injury crisis is finally calming down, with Mile Svilar and Paulo Dybala making their comebacks at the weekend, where Malen scored four goals in a 5-1 drubbing of Parma.

However, Malen and Dybala do not start in Paris, as Niccolò Pisilli is drafted in to bolster the midfield with Soulé and Koné.

Santiago Castro therefore leads the attack instead, perhaps hoping to tire PSG out before unleashing their biggest talents, seeing as Roma have shown a tendency to fall away.

Marten de Roon is also preferred to Bryan Cristante in the midfield.

Devyne Rensch and Lorenzo Pellegrini are the only remaining absentees.

Paris Saint-Germain won the last two editions of the Champions League, but their chances of a hat-trick have been badly damaged by losing two stars for the rest of the season.

Just weeks after former Napoli hero Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tore his anterior cruciate ligament, Désiré Doué suffered the same fate.

This is a special fixture for coach Luis Enrique, who started his senior management career at Roma in 2011/12.

There are other familiar faces, as Marquinhos was at Roma in 2012/13, while Fabian Ruiz made his name at Napoli and Achraf Hakimi first shone for Inter.

PSG need to reshuffle with Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos dropped, so Maghnes Alkiouche, Ferran Torres and Senny Mayulu all start together.

PSG: Safonov; Hakimi, Zabarnyi, Willian Pacho, Nuno Mendes; Joao Neves, Vitinha, Fabian Ruiz; Akliouche, Ferran Torres, Mayulu

PSG bench: Chevalier, Bar, Lucas Beraldo, Marquinhos, Dembele, Digne, Lucas Hernandez, Godts, Dro Fernandez, Zaire-Emery, Boly, Ndjantou

Roma: Svilar; Mancini, N’Dicka, Hermoso; Wesley, De Roon, Koné, Molina; Soulé, Pisilli; Castro

Roma bench: De Marzi, Gollini, Koulierakis, Cristante, Malen, Dybala, Balerdi, Lulli, Rodrigo Mora, Ghilardi

#1194. James Penrice warns Rangers they must improve if they intend to hit the Scottish Premiership summit

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 10:26 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 10:37 EST, 25 November 2026

James Penrice has warned that Rangers can forget about going top of the table on Saturday if they play like they did for the first 45 minutes against Aberdeen.

Derek McInnes’ side were a goal down at half-time and heading to their first defeat in 14 games after failing to get going against the Dons.

With the manager making three changes at half-time, the Ibrox men scored three times in an incredible 11-minute burst through Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin.

And while Aberdeen netted again via Findlay Marshall, Rangers hung on for the win which put them within a point of Celtic.

With the leaders facing Hearts at Tynecastle on Sunday, McInnes’ men can move to the summit if they defeat high-flying Falkirk the day before. But Penrice says that will only happen if they deliver a more complete display than they showed on Tuesday.

‘It’s a massive incentive for us, but the league isn’t won in November,’ said the defender. ‘Falkirk are playing well. They’ve travelled well away from home too.

James Penrice has warned Rangers they will need to improve if they are to take top spot

‘We’ll need to be on it. We can’t go into that game like we did on Tuesday night. I wouldn’t say we were lucky, but we can’t concede two goals at home. We can’t do that on Saturday.

‘Is it important we grab that chance (to go top)? Definitely. We’ll just concentrate on ourselves. It’s another game to tick off and we’ll turn up hoping to get the three points.’

McInnes introduced Tuur Rommens, Findlay Curtis and Kim Min-su at the break with the changes leading to a much-improved display.

Despite chalking up the win which maintained the unbeaten run, Penrice insists the overall show left considerable room for improvement.

‘It was very mixed,’ he reflected. ‘We concede in the first half, but then fly out the traps in the second.

‘I thought we were really good for 20 minutes. We go and score a third and look comfortable. But then we switch off. We turned our back at a free-kick and they end up scoring. We made it difficult for ourselves.

‘But we got three goals. Ryan got his usual one where he’s alive in the box. Gas was brilliant and he got his goal then Nico got his. But again, we made it hard for ourselves. The main thing is we got three points.

‘We made a few changes at half-time and I thought the boys who came on were brilliant. They had that real spark and energy. We started the second half really well but, ultimately, we need to score more.

Rangers goalscorers Djeidi Gassama, Nico Raskin and Ryan Naderi celebrate against Aberdeen

‘We could have done that and made it easy for ourselves.’

Rangers haven’t now tasted defeat since losing away to Czech side Jablonec on August 27. And while not every display in that run has been outstanding, Penrice is encouraged by the fact that the team is showing plenty of character.

‘We’ve shown we’ve got a bit of resilience,’ he said. ‘It’s not a bad trait to be winning games and scoring late on. We’re doing that. But as players we want to make the game as easy as possible.

‘We’re on a run just now and hopefully it continues.

‘The positives on Tuesday night were that, in spells, we were really good. We were flying in the second half. But we can’t concede two goals at home and expect to always come away with a win.’

Meanwhile, Penrice says he’s got no fears that Min-su will become a goal threat for the team.

The South Korean, an £8.5million summer signing from Girona, has yet to find the net in 14 appearances with his sole assist coming against Motherwell last Saturday.

The forward thought he’d broken his duck with a spectacular late effort against the Dons only for the ball to sail over.

‘I said to Min-su at full-time that me and big Ryan were ready to run to him at 100mph if he’d scored that goal,’ Penrice smiled.

‘You can see he wants it so bad. He probably just needs to calm down in front of goal.

‘I thought that was the one when he chopped inside. I thought he was scoring, but he put it into row Z.

Kim Min-su has impressed for Rangers but is still waiting to score his first goal for the club

‘It wasn’t ideal, but he was still happy afterward because we won the game.

‘You can see in his game that, at every opportunity, he’s trying to get a shot away. It will come and hopefully it comes at a perfect time.

‘There’s a reason these players are at Ibrox — it’s because they’re extremely talented. It’s just that last bit but they’re very young.

‘Min-su’s game isn’t just goals and assists. He’s a really talented footballer who creates problems for teams. He’s been a massive part of why we’re on this run. You can all see it.

‘It’s about more than goals and assists, but if he adds that to his game, he’s only going to go on and have a very successful career.

‘That’s what the boys want for him. We want our wide players and strikers to score as many as possible.’

#1193. Amorim: ‘Milan must do well in Europa League and Serie A, only way to be a good team’

Ruben Amorim warns Olympiacos are ‘aggressive, especially at home’ in the Europa League, but Milan ‘have to do well both in the League and in Europe, it’s the only way to be a good team.’

It kicks off in Athens on Thursday at 17.45 GMT (18.45 CET).

Injuries are piling up for this trip, with Luka Modric, Strahinja Pavlovic, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi joining Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Fikayo Tomori, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Pietro Terracciano on the treatment table.

At least Mike Maignan is available again after suspension, and confidence was boosted by a 5-1 Serie A victory over Frosinone.

“It’s a fact that we need to improve in the final third,” said Amorim in his press conference.

“The only thing we can do is improve our principles. We need to improve on these little things, and that’s the only way I can help my players. Against Olympiacos, it will be a different match than the one against Frosinone, just as it will be different than the one against Cagliari.

“We need to improve, even in our defending. We’ve almost always conceded a goal, so that’s another area we need to improve.”

Olympiacos are sixth in the Europa League table after amassing 10 points from four games, beating Jagiellonia, Olympique Marseille and Sparta Prague before the 0-0 draw away to Stade Rennais.

Notably, they have conceded only one goal in those four matches.

“They’re a strong team. They’re aggressive, especially at home. I’ve played here twice, and it was tough for me. I know their coach and what he wants to do. They play compact, positive football, 4-3-3, they change a lot, they rotate, they have Jota, a lot of Portuguese players.

“They’re a strong team, and with their fans there, it’ll be a tough match. Chiquinho is a great talent, but very impulsive. I hope he plays well tomorrow, but I hope he still has a great career ahead of him.”

The Rossoneri’s form in the Europa League has been little short of disastrous, as the 4-0 victory away to RB Salzburg was an outlier between three defeats to Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, all without scoring a single goal.

“To be a good team, you have to do well both in the league and in Europe,” insisted Amorim.

“That’s the only way to be a good team. We have to be, especially at Milan. I’m always waiting for things to go badly, because it doesn’t take much to change the situation. That’s what I’m trying to make my players understand, because it won’t always be this way. We’re at the beginning of a process, and I think we need everyone.

“We lost Pavlovic, Modric, Saelemaekers, Chukwueze, and everyone has to be ready, because there are no excuses at big clubs. We have to be ready for this. I can’t believe we lost all these games in Europe because we rotated.

“We have to always be ready and approach the games like against Inter, Frosinone, and Genoa. We’re building so many things. Tomorrow is another test for us.”

Does Amorim still believe that Milan will be able to challenge for the Scudetto?

“I haven’t changed my mind. This year is difficult, but if we have the chance to fight, we’ll do it.”

Many coaches have been asked about the release of the Grand Theft Auto VI game and how much time players are committing to it.

“I’d rather my players play that every day rather than scroll through social media,” replied Amorim.

“Social media, and all that stuff, is very difficult for players, who in any case live with more criticism than I do. After Frosinone, I haven’t read anything, because that’s how I want to live my life.”

#1192. Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide1,2,3,4, yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999–2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species’ elevational ranges: upper portions of species’ ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

Shifts in the distribution of tree species in response to climate change1,2 and disturbances3,4 can substantially affect forest structure, biodiversity and ecosystem services5,6,7,8. Such redistribution can be characterized by shifts in tree abundance centres, which reveals how populations reorganize within their ranges2,9,10. Given that cooler conditions occur at higher latitudes and elevations, poleward and upslope shifts in species distribution are expected with climate change1,9,10,11,12. However, downslope shifts of tree species in montane ecosystems have also been reported, probably reflecting the influence of non-temperature factors that alter tree abundance and distribution in contrasting ways13,14,15,16. Natural disturbances, such as wildfires, diseases and insect outbreaks, along with subsequent regeneration, can alter stem abundance and basal area (the cross-sectional surface area of tree trunks measured at breast height—1.37 m above the ground) across regions4, influencing latitudinal or longitudinal shifts3. Yet, the roles of disturbances in shaping species’ elevational redistribution remains underexplored8.

Forests in the western USA span a broad elevational range, from near sea level to approximately 3,700 m, near the upper treeline. Over recent decades, these forests have experienced pronounced warming and frequent droughts17,18, which have increased wildfire activity19,20 and insect outbreaks21,22, and altered forest disease patterns22,23. As these disturbances can alter tree demographic dynamics4, elevational variation in disturbance activity may drive the elevational redistribution of tree abundance. Moreover, warming may shift disturbance patterns23,24,25, further influencing tree abundance redistribution. Although previous studies have reported elevational shifts across regions, most have been restricted geographically with inconsistent patterns9,14,26,27,28. A comprehensive and cross-regional assessment using a consistent methodology remains lacking, which limits our understanding of elevational shift patterns and their underlying mechanisms in the context of environmental change.

To fill this gap, we quantified elevational shifts in tree abundance centres of common tree species across individual ecosections (ecoregion sections) in the western USA using remeasured plots conducted by the US Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) programme29. As the western USA spans a vast climatic and ecological gradient and encompasses diverse forest types, estimating elevational shifts across the entire region would mask regional-scale differences and could be confounded by species’ geographical redistribution among regions14,30,31,32. We therefore conducted our analyses separately within individual ecosections for each species. By selecting tree species that occurred in more than 100 remeasured FIA plots without evidence of silvicultural treatment within individual montane ecosections (Fig. 1a), we identified 45 species (Extended Data Table 1) across 33 ecosections, yielding 212 species–ecosection combinations. Collectively, they accounted for 68% of total stems and 69% of total basal area across montane forests in the western USA.

The proportions of total stems or basal area with significant downslope (brown) and upslope (green) shifts are annotated. c, Mean shift rates in individual ecosections, weighted by basal area (left) and stem abundance (right) across species. Light blue shading is to distinguish ecoregion provinces. d, Mean shift rates for each species, weighted by basal area (left) and stem abundance (right) across ecosections.
