#1143. Trinity Rodman's non-negotiable for Washington Spirit: 'I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – For 90 minutes, dedication to an organized plan is the default state for soccer players, but a postmatch celebration always has a randomness to it. Players and team staff scatter around a field and seem to bump into each other by coincidence, a sense of enthusiastic spontaneity coming over a wide variety of people. There was no actual shock in the fact that Trinity Rodman ran into Washington Spirit owner Michele Kang after their win over the Utah Royals in the NWSL semifinals last week. The sheer joy of reaching a third straight NWSL Championship, though, took over.

Rodman jumped on Kang from behind, and the owner delighted in the surprise. The multimillionaire, clad in a chic gray cape that embodies a dignified but serious demeanor, then wasted no time clasping her hands with Rodman's and bouncing up and down. Sports team owners are hardly ever caught so candidly; no matter how much attention they do or do not attract, they are the resident corporate types, the odd ones out next to a bunch of athletes by design. For a moment on Saturday, though, Kang and Rodman were one and the same.

LITERAL GOALS.Michele Kang and Trinity Rodman celebrating the Spirit way 💃 pic.twitter.com/RpTMKhTeLd

It was a perfect peek inside Rodman's orbit.

Rodman does not lack the seriousness that Kang exudes, her commitment to her craft just as evident as her skill. She is open to any and all questions about her job, whether they are very literally about soccer or about the nature of being the NWSL's brightest star, but not ones about aliens, which she made very clear in an interaction with a content creator on Thursday. There is a non-negotiable that's just as essential to Rodman's game as her clinical instincts in front of goal, one that is crucial to her appeal -- having fun.

"I just think you shouldn't be doing anything if you're not having fun," she said Thursday, two days before playing in her fourth NWSL Championship with the Spirit. "I think I wouldn't be playing soccer if it wasn't fun for me, so sometimes it is hard to show it and to experience it because you are so focused and there is a lot of pressure, but I'm hoping to always be that person that allows us to let loose."

Five years after winning the NWSL Championship at the end of a Rookie of the Year campaign, Rodman is no stranger to the league's showpiece match. The Spirit are now the finalists for a third season in a row and are still in the midst of chasing their first title since 2021, but even amid the familiarity, this year is notably different from the last. This time last year, the Spirit's headliner was battling an injury in the run-up to the final and was in the middle of negotiating what would later become a historic contract in women's soccer. She carries none of that baggage this time around.

"I'm so excited," she said. "I think going into a championship is obviously always a blessing, but going into it not 100% isn't the greatest feeling because you know that you're still going to play, but you don't know if it's going to be a great performance, so I think to be healthy and to be able to give everything that I have is really exciting for me as an individual, but also to be able to contribute to the team and get these minutes in for the last hurrah."

Rodman has played 32 times this season and averaged 86.6 minutes per game along the way, an upgrade from 2025's tally of 17 matches and an average of 56.8 minutes per game during an injury-riddled campaign. It has allowed the 24-year-old to set the tone on the pitch, as well as off it.

"She's bubbly and brings energy to the changing room," defender Esme Morgan said, speaking in the build-up to the game. "She always comes in on game day and kind of screams as she enters the changing room so you're like, 'Oh, Trin's arrived.'"

There's a playfulness to Rodman that is matched by the team as a whole, so much so that, on the drive to the team's training facility in Leesburg, Va., Morgan contemplates a list of questions that feels unique to the Spirit.

"I am excited to go in every day," Morgan said. "I drive into training, and I'm looking forward to seeing the girls, and I'm thinking, 'What stupid conversation are we going to have today? What are we going to laugh about today? What silly thing are we going to do?'"

"We have these big red gym balls in the gym, like exercise balls, and we enjoy kind of throwing them at each other, whacking them off each other so it can get very silly," Morgan said. "I did accidentally knock [Gabrielle] Carle off one. She was bouncing on the gym ball, and I smashed one. I was aiming for a member of staff, actually. I kicked it and then missed him slightly, bounced off the wall, hit Gabby Carle, and she fell off her exercise balls, so it was funny. She was completely fine. No Gabby Carles were harmed, but that was funny, so yeah, we've been kind of going crazy with the exercise balls."

Then there's Jose the Coyote, a plastic good-luck charm that is emblematic of Rodman's non-negotiable.

"I think just finding little things to get excited about, if it's as simple as Jose the Coyote," Rodman said. "Just latching onto little things that we can joke around about or have fun with, but honestly, we've been having a great time. We've been growing closer, and I think even just how many new players we've had join the roster, I think, has almost brought us closer because we do need to have more unity and language barrier and everything forces us to be closer, so I think the close-knit group allows us to have a lot more fun because we're comfortable."

The joy is naturally rooted in something much deeper, if equally simple, after injuries have restricted her ability to focus on the task at hand.

"I think I'm just having fun in general," she noted, "because I'm playing so that's fun for me."

Kang's interaction with Rodman at Audi Field last weekend is the type of thing that comes up in conversation unprompted, in large part because it is a snapshot of the Spirit as a club.

"Here are arguably the two people who have built us into this incredible organization with massive success," Spirit CEO Kim Stone said. "It's because of the two of them. Trinity invests on the pitch. Michele invests in everything else ... [Rodman is] the only person who can jump up on Michele Kang and get her to dance and not get a different reaction from Michele."

Before Rodman officially signed a deal in January worth $2 million annually, there was no question that she was worth every penny. The player is "baked into" every layer of the club's business, per Stone -- season tickets, single-game tickets, jersey sales, viewership, you name it. She is the type of player the NWSL, with much hand-wringing and a new construct following a back-and-forth with the Players Association, built a whole new rule around. It is formally called the High Impact Player rule; in conversation, in headlines and on Wikipedia, it is known as the Rodman rule. A year ago, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman used her state of the league address to say the league would "fight" to keep Rodman around as part of a larger effort to sign and retain stars. Berman took her victory lap on Thursday ahead of another glittery NWSL Championship.

"Obviously, it was incredibly important for us to keep Trinity in this league," she said. "The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field and we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her story and candidly, it's our job to continue to create more of those stories so that other people are just as excited about all of the stars that do play in the NWSL."

Rodman, though, is singular in her value to the NWSL.

"She's baked into the fact that we get asked to play Denver [Summit] in front of 60,000 people, to play Bay FC at Oracle Park, to play [in] New York for the Queens Classic," Stone noted. "If you look at all the milestone attendance, look who the opponent is. It's every time and so she's baked into all of that. I can't quantify that off the top of my head but what I can tell you is, when I worked with Miami Heat, we had LeBron James and then when I was at Golden State [Warriors], we had Steph Curry and those generational talents, what they do for your entire organization, especially when you have a good attitude and personality like Trinity, like Steph Curry, they transform your org.

It all comes down to Rodman's non-negotiable, something that will soon become a trademark as much as the goal contributions if it is not already.

"She's fun, she's engaging," Stone said. "She's what people want to be around and they're drawn to and then she's phenomenal with fans ... If you have a personality, then we can help amplify what you're trying to do. If you are vanilla ice cream, I'm going to struggle to get a lot of people interested. If you're rocky road fudge sundae with caramel pecans on top, I got something to work with. I got some unique things. I got some fun stuff to do because what people want is just the authenticity."

Rodman has earned the right to be the NWSL's transformational, singular talent, successfully receiving a torch that was left behind a few years ago by members of the 2019 Women's World Cup-winning U.S. team that captivated a nation.

"Trin is a generational talent," Stone said. "She transcends soccer. She is arguably the face of soccer in America, men's or women's, hard stop ... What you end up with is the most popular player in our league, the most sold jerseys in our league. The people used to shout for Alex Morgan. Now they're all shouting for Trinity."

#1142. Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot–superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man’s Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron–hole character, but lack topological protection3,4,5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man’s Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6,7,8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man’s Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains.

Wiring diagram for the DC and RF lines used to measure the device, with properties and components detailed in the legend. Additional details can be found in ‘Measurement set-up’ in Methods.

a, Detailed schematic of the pulse sequence, showing the various stages of the protocol. b, p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of pulse duration and pulse ramp time. Parity oscillations remain visible even for slow ramp duration up to approximately 75 ns. An oscillation as a function of ramp duration is also visible at zero pulse duration, indicating that the qubit evolves partially during the ramp of the coupling pulse. c, Time trace and corresponding histogram of the readout signal \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) with the left chain on resonance and the right-chain QDs off-resonance, using 400 μs readout time. Transitions between \(| e\rangle \) and \(| o\rangle \) are attributed to quasiparticle poisoning. d, Dwell time histogram from c. e, p(e∣e), p(o∣e), p(e∣o), and p(o∣o) while varying the pulse amplitude VC and ramp time. For fast ramps (≲5 ns), parity mixing is observed between the chain and the dot. We attribute this to a diabatic excitation of the coupled system, which rapidly decoheres before the final measurement. In the main text, we use ramp times of 25 ns to avoid these excitations. For pulse amplitudes ≲11.5 mV, no parity mixing is observed, which we use to roughly identify when QDC passes through resonance. f, Schematic of the configuration for the measurements in c-e. g-j, Same as c-f, but for the right chain, with the QDs of the left chain off-resonance. In panel i, parity mixing between the chain and QDC is observed for ramp times  ≲ 10 ns, indicating a slightly weaker coupling between QDC and the right chain versus the left chain.

Readout characterization using time traces of the reflected resonator signal \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\), measured for three different amounts of detuning with the coupler QD kept fixed far from resonance. Thresholds used for single-shot state identification are obtained by fitting a Gaussian mixture model. The detuning configuration in (e-g) is used for qubit readout. a, Schematic representation of the readout configuration with both chains on resonance. b, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in a. Residual coupling between the chains results in inter-chain hopping that is faster than the readout time of 500 μs, preventing readout in a single shot. The two quantum capacitance signals corresponding to the \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) states are partially averaged which makes them difficult to distinguish from the \(| oe\rangle \) and \(| eo\rangle \) states. c, As in a, but with both chains detuned from resonance. d, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in c. The slight detuning suppresses inter-chain hopping, though it remains too fast for high-fidelity single-shot readout. Two distinctive regions can be observed: When the system is in the global even state, rapid jumps between \(| oo\rangle \) and \(| ee\rangle \) are visible. When the system is poisoned, it enters the global odd manifold. Transitions between \(| oe\rangle \) and \(| eo\rangle \) are not resolved because they produce similar readout signals. e, As in c but with both chains detuned further from resonance. f, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in e. The two computational states \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) correspond to the red and blue signals, and can now clearly be resolved. The green signal contains both leakage states of the odd global parity manifold (\(| eo\rangle \) and \(| oe\rangle \)). Due to the antisymmetric detuning where the ground state of one dot is full and the other is empty, the \(| oo\rangle \) state is energetically favored over the \(| ee\rangle \) state, resulting in a skewed population between the two. Transitions are mainly observed between the even and odd global manifolds. The signal-to-noise ratios between the leakage distribution and the \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) distributions are 2.88 ± 0.28 and 2.76 ± 0.09, respectively. Integrating the fitted Gaussian distributions across the assignment thresholds gives false-leakage probabilities of 0.45% for \(| ee\rangle \) and 0.25% for \(| oo\rangle \), showing that finite readout SNR accounts for only a small fraction of the observed leakage. g, Dwell time histogram of the three observed states, indicating the difference in lifetimes. The shortest measured state lifetime in this readout configuration is 8.3 ms, corresponding to a probability of approximately 5.8% for a state transition during the 500 μs integration window. The trace is acquired with the coupler QD kept far from resonance, showing that state switching on this timescale is already present in the readout configuration. These transitions include both residual inter-chain hopping and quasiparticle-poisoning events and can produce time-averaged signals that are assigned as leakage for pulsed measurements.

Conditional probabilities at the simultaneous sweet spot for the two chains in both the even and odd global parity manifolds, corresponding to Extended Data Fig. 5g but extended to larger pulse amplitudes. Additional outer lines appear when the energy of the detuned chain is aligned with the first excited state of the other chain. The quadrant in which they appear depends on the initial state of the system, as well as the global parity manifold (‘Interpretation of pulsed charge-stability diagrams’ in Methods). a, Left chain in the even manifold. b, Right chain in the even manifold. c, Left chain in the odd manifold. d, Right chain in the odd manifold. The QDR2 resonance is shifted by approximately 3 mV with respect to panel b due to the Coulomb interaction with the additional electron on the parity-switching QD. The odd-manifold measurements include two parity-switch passages, before and after the control sequence. Comparing the background return probabilities in the even- and odd-manifold measurements for initial states \(| oo\rangle \) and \(| oe\rangle \) gives single-passage parity-switch fidelity of 99.77 ± 0.03% (‘Parity-switch fidelity’ in Methods).

a, Map of p(oo∣oo) (left) and p(oe∣oe) (right) as a function of the left and right hybrid-gate voltages (VLH and VRH). The diagonal and antidiagonal features of enhanced parity mixing correspond to degeneracies between the qubit basis states. The points labeled c-k indicate the VLH,VRH values used in the remaining panels. b, Schematic representation of the four configurations measured at each point: left- and right-chain pulsed charge-stability diagrams in the global even and odd parity manifolds. c-k, Pulsed charge-stability diagrams measured for the left and right chains in the even (top) and odd (bottom) parity manifolds. Unlike conventional charge-stability diagrams referenced to the Fermi energy in a normal lead, here each chain provides the energy reference for the other. As such, the measured features reflect the difference between the excitation energies of the two individual chains. Crossings are therefore observed simultaneously for the left and right chains when the splittings of the two chains compensate each other, corresponding to the qubit degeneracy condition. Consequently, the appearance of a crossing in a single parity manifold does not imply that the corresponding chain is tuned to its sweet spot. Indeed, crossing-like features are observed in only one manifold in panels c, e, i and k. The orientation of the avoided crossings depends on the parity manifold: in the even manifold, the left and right chains exhibit the same orientation, whereas in the odd manifold the orientation is reversed, reflecting the sign difference ε12 ± ε34 between the two manifolds. Only near the sweet spot (panel g) are crossings observed for both chains in both parity manifolds simultaneously, providing a unique signature that both chains are individually tuned to their sweet spots.

Pulsed charge-stability diagrams showing p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of the right-chain gate voltages (VR1, VR2), for various values of the coupler QD pulse amplitude VC for a fixed pulse duration of 10 ns. The value of VC is indicated above each panel. The device configuration is the same as in Extended Data Fig. 8. a-h, The superconducting phase difference between the chains is set to φ ≈ 0. As VC is made more negative, the coupler QD is first brought closer to resonance and parity mixing along the degeneracy lines increases. Eventually, when the coupler QD is near or below resonance (around VC = − 9 mV), the final state is dictated by the ground state of the chain in the relevant sector of the charge-stability diagram irrespective of the initial state. We note that the chain appears to move from CAR-like at low pulse amplitudes (tR < ΔR, a) across a sweet spot (tR ≈ ΔR, b-e) to ECT-like at high pulse amplitudes (tR > ΔR, f-h), which we attribute to uncompensated cross-capacitance between VC and VRH. i-n, The superconducting phase difference between the chains is set to φ ≈ π. The main difference is that the visibility of QDR2 is suppressed, as predicted by theory (Supplementary Note 4).

p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of pulse duration for various detunings, as indicated by the schematics, corresponding to measurements shown in the main text. Unless stated otherwise, measurements are taken at VC = 9.8 mV and perpendicular field B⊥ = 15.6 mT (yellow mark in panel o), corresponding to a phase difference φ ≈ 0 between the chains. a-d, Detuning individual quantum dots. e,f, Detuning the left- (e) and right-chain QDs (f). g,h, Simultaneous detuning of the outer (g) and inner (h) QDs of both chains. i, Varying coupling pulse duration and amplitude. j, Varying VLH and VRH for a fixed pulse duration of 18 ns. The colored marks indicate sweep directions for panels k,l,p,q. k,l, Detuning the left (k) and right (l) chain via VLH and VRH. m, Oscillation frequency as a function of pulse amplitude in logarithmic scale, where V0 is the gate voltage at which QDC is on resonance. The gray line fits f = K/(V0 − VC) with K = 156.6 ± 0.3 MHz mV and V0 = 11.285 ± 0.002 mV for VC < 10.8 mV. n, Quality factor of the oscillations as a function of VC. o, Dependence on the out-of-plane magnetic field B⊥. p,q, Symmetric (p) and antisymmetric (q) detuning of VLH together with VRH.

p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of pulse duration for various detunings, as indicated by the schematics. Note that for this dataset, the chains were tuned using pulsed charge-stability diagrams but were not compared to the odd manifold. As such, it is unclear if the even and odd states of each chain are degenerate. a, Varying coupling pulse duration and amplitude VC. In contrast to the main text, QDC starts detuned below the Fermi level instead of above but is likewise pulsed closer to resonance for qubit evolution. b, Dependence on the out-of-plane magnetic field B⊥. In this case, we observe decoherence around φ = π (B⊥ ≈ 13.5 mT), consistent with a small residual detuning of an outer QD from resonance; such detuning restores transverse coupling near φ ≈ π (Supplementary Note 4). c,d, Detuning the left (c) and right (d) chain via VLH and VRH. e-h, Single-dot detuning of VL1, VL2, VR1 and VR2. i,j, Detuning the left- (i) and right-chain QDs (j). k,l, Simultaneous detuning of the outer (k) and inner (l) quantum dots of both chains.

p(eo∣eo), p(oe∣oe), p(eo∣oe), and p(oe∣eo) as a function of pulse duration for various detunings, as indicated by the schematics, corresponding to measurements shown in the main text. a, Varying coupling pulse duration and amplitude VC. b,c, Detuning the left (b) and right (c) chain via VLH and VRH. d, Varying VLH and VRH for a fixed pulse duration of 18 ns. The colored marks indicate sweep directions for panels b,c,e,f. e,f, Symmetric (e) and antisymmetric (f) detuning of VLH together with VRH. g-i, Oscillation frequency (g), Rabi decay time \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) (h) and quality factor Q (i) extracted from panel a as a function of VC.

Extracted Rabi coherence time \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) for the different detuning configurations shown in Fig. 4, as indicated by the schematics. a-d, Detuning individual quantum dots. e,f, Detuning the left (e) and right (f) Kitaev chains. g,h, Simultaneous detuning of the outer (g) and inner (h) quantum dots of both chains. Gray markers indicate fits for which the relative uncertainty in \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) exceeds 50% or the fitted oscillation frequency lies outside the 10–200 MHz range, and are therefore considered unreliable. For visibility, the \({T}_{2}^{{\rm{Rabi}}}\) axis is also limited to 40 ns. Fitted values beyond this range are not shown, as they also arise from unreliable fits and are not physically meaningful. The same-chain two-dot detunings show the narrowest range over which coherent oscillations can be reliably fitted, whereas the single-dot and cross-chain detunings retain resolvable oscillations over a broader range. The simultaneous two-dot detunings in panels e-h use the same voltage scales as the corresponding single-dot measurements in panels a-d, and the pulse amplitude applied to the second quantum dot is shown on the upper axis.

#1141. Real Madrid tie Tchouaméni and Güler to 2032 contracts within 24 hours

Real Madrid have extended the contracts of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Arda Güler until June 2032, a day apart. With captain Fede Valverde also reportedly agreeing new terms, the club are securing their core midfield for years to come.

Real Madrid have committed two midfield regulars to long-term deals in the space of 24 hours. Güler’s announcement came first, and Aurélien Tchouaméni’s followed.

Both players are part of the core of Mourinho’s midfield. The renewals keep them at the club for six more seasons.

Tchouaméni arrived in 2022 and has made 205 appearances for the club. He has won eight trophies in that time. They include one Champions League, two Club World Cups and two UEFA Super Cups. He has also lifted one LaLiga, one Copa del Rey and one Spanish Super Cup.

His standing goes beyond the club. He has 50 France caps and won the 2021 Nations League. The new contract is worth around €9 million net per season, GOAL reported. The agreement came after interest from Manchester United.

Güler’s record covers a shorter spell. He was 18 when he joined. He has 38 caps for Turkey. In September he was named Breakthrough Player of the 2025-26 Champions League. His new salary is reportedly about €8m a year.

The two profiles differ. Tchouaméni is an established international with a full set of club honours. Güler is a younger player whose contract now runs almost nine years from his arrival. Tying both to the same end date suggests a midfield the club intend to keep together.

The club may not be finished. Captain Fede Valverde has agreed to extend his contract from 2029 to 2031, according to GOAL. The new deal will make him one of the squad’s highest earners. An announcement is expected soon, as Madrid work on further renewals after Güler and Tchouaméni.

If Valverde’s extension is confirmed, none of the three midfielders would have a contract ending before 2031. That would remove contract questions over a key part of the squad for several seasons. The two completed renewals arrived during the build-up to a busy run of home matches.

🚨🤍 Aurelien Tchouameni has signed new long term deal at Real Madrid until June 2032. pic.twitter.com/13BtcLyubP

— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 19, 2026

Tchouaméni has not been fully clear of fitness concerns this month. Earlier in November he left the France squad with a muscle problem. He was back in training with the Madrid squad on the day his renewal was announced.

Real Madrid host Celta at the Santiago Bernabéu on Saturday 21 November at 21:00 in LaLiga matchday 13. PSV then visit for a Champions League game on Tuesday 24 November.

#1140. Five European teams to watch as Mauricio Pochettino begins Manchester United era

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The international break is over, and it's now time to get back to the usual business with European soccer resuming alongside the MLS playoffs in the United States. It was supposed to be a quiet break, but that wasn't the case at all, since Manchester United decided to part ways with Michael Carrick and appointed Mauricio Pochettino, who had recently signed a new deal with the United States men's national team but decided to leave after the break. Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid will battle with Barcelona for the LaLiga title, while Como are still one of the most interesting sides to watch in the near future. Let's now take a look at the five teams to watch after the break, starting with the Red Devils.

The biggest change of the break: Manchester United sacked coach and club legend Michael Carrick and replaced him with Pochettino, who makes his Premier League comeback after coaching Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. As the English giants are currently sitting 18th in the standings, this is a major task for the now-former USMNT head coach, who will make his return at Anfield against Liverpool in his opening game at United. It's a daunting start in one of the most hostile atmospheres in the country. For Pochettino, the challenge will be to strike the right balance between delivering short-term results and laying the foundations for a new chapter at the club. His ambition will be to usher in a fresh cycle at an institution that has endured one crisis after another since Sir Alex Ferguson stepped down more than a decade ago.

Speaking of a former Manchester United head coach, Jose Mourinho has had some ups and downs early in his first season back at Real Madrid. After winning an exciting away El Clasico match against Barcelona, Mourinho's team is only three points behind Hansi Flick's side right now and is eyeing the possibility of challenging them for the LaLiga title this season. They certainly have all the ingredients to make it happen, particularly following some remarkable additions to the squad in the summer of 2026. Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham are arguably entering their prime and appear ready to take the team to the next level, supported by a number of exciting young prospects who could play a key role in shaping the club's future. Will Mourinho be able to win a trophy in his first season back at the club? That would be a story.

If there is one team to watch in Serie A, it's Como. The side led by Cesc Fabregas is impressing both domestically and in Europe, as it is currently fourth in the league-phase standings of the UEFA Champions League. Fabregas can count on some of the best players in the league, such as Nico Paz, the Argentine talent who is now also expected to lead the national team after Lionel Messi's retirement. The question is how far Como can go this season, given that playing every three days can be a big challenge for players who have never experienced it. They may still have to pay the price in the league, but qualifying for at least the playoffs of Europe's elite competition would remain a realistic target and, given the circumstances, a remarkable achievement in itself.

It's always about Manchester City: the Citizens are still waiting to learn what sanctions they will face after an independent commission found them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. They are facing a challenging season that might have an impact on the years ahead. It's not clear what the sanctions will be, but we will likely know more before the end of the current season. On the pitch, they are also facing a season of changes as longtime coach Pep Guardiola left the club in the summer and was replaced by Enzo Maresca, who is now overseeing that transition.

Spanish soccer is not just about Real Madrid and Barcelona: Atletico Madrid are once again near the top of the standings, five points behind the Blaugrana. Diego Simeone, who has coached the club since 2011, is an Atletico Madrid legend who has faced so many changes over the years but has always been able to recreate the right atmosphere and environment to succeed. Atletico have changed their tactical approach and playing style many times, but they are still near the top, and that is what makes Simeone special.

#1139. Sporting Lisbon vs Manchester United RECAP: Visitors held in controversial and chaotic thriller as Liverpool beat Club Brugge

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER and LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER

Relive Daily Mail Sport's coverage from Wednesday's Champions League action as Manchester United travelled to Sporting Lisbon while Liverpool took on Club Brugge.

It's not every day that you get to spend an evening with Harry Bamforth and Luke Power - and we wouldn't recommend it, either.

Thanks for putting up with us, especially when the football is hard enough to cope with as it is if you're a Manchester United fan.

Do joins us in the morning as the reaction and fall-out from the Champions League action continues interminably.

Here are the Premier League fixtures at the weekend:

Senne Lammens' two errors cost Man United victory at Sporting

CHRIS WHEELER AT JOSE ALVALADE STADIUM: A week into the job and Mauricio Pochettino must be getting used to the madness of Manchester United.

Liverpool showed a bit of everything tonight: possession dominance in the first half, counter-attacking prowess in the second, and defensive solidity throughout (for the most part!).

Lewis Steele was on hand to bring you his thoughts from Belgium.

Club Brugge 0-3 Liverpool: Reds close in on qualification

LEWIS STEELE AT JAN BREYDEL STADION: A brace for Isak and another from Wirtz fired the Reds to victory in Bruges after their strikes helped Liverpool get back to winning ways in Europe.

Normally I post all the goals and crazy moments separately, but there were just too many tonight.

So, instead, you can catch all the chaos in the highlights on YouTube. From penalties and howlers to disallowed goals and sending-offs, this game had it all.

Rio Ngumoha is averaging 7.8 completed dribbles every match in this year's Champions League.

No player with at least 300 minutes played has done better since 2006-07. Full credit to Opta for this one. One man has done more this campaign, and that's Jeremy Doku on 11.9, but he doesn't have the 300 minutes under his belt.

Let it sink in. When we think of direct, unstoppable dribblers, we think of Lionel Messi, Neymar, Khvichia Kvaratskhelia. Oddly Thomas Partey was up there in the standings one season. But those world-class wingers, Ngumoha is up there with them for pure dribbling ability at the moment. It's a long career ahead, and you hope his spark won't be muted, but he has mad a dazzling start. If he can add goals and assists, his potential is sky-high.

Manchester United may have been done over by some decisions, I know, but not all of them were wrong.

The penalty conceded by Senne Lammens? Stonewall.

So that means the next stat I am about to share is a pretty damning indictment of United's season (bar the Leny Yoro red, before you all have a pop at me).

Man United have received five red cards and conceded five penalties in just 17 games across all competitions this season.

Liverpool couldn't have had a better week going into the Merseyside derby than beating Manchester United and Brugge 7-0 on aggregate.

The annoying thing for Andoni Iraola is that Victor Munoz has picked up a knock, and he had to bring on Rio Ngumoha earlier than expected as a result, so that inhibits his options and energy up front ever so slightly.

But he will be greatly encouraged by how his £100m+ men, namely Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, and Bradley Barcola, are melding. We're yet to see the best from the latter on a consistent basis. That's the final piece of the puzzle.

Wirtz is flying now - he has now scored or assisted or done both in seven of his last nine games in the Premier League and Champions League.

Everton are having a good season and will be right up for it, but Liverpool have teed themselves up for a good performance at midday on Sunday.

Mauricio Pochettino, Man United boss, speaking to TNT Sports:

Here's the Alisson assist from earlier. Playmaker stuff from Liverpool's number one. Always thought he could have played outfield.

Manchester United just hate playing away in Europe.

United are now winless in their last seven Champions League away games (D3 L4).

Their worst-ever run is eight... which they could well match after playing their final away match in the league phase in January.

#1138. Roberto Fernández goal earns Eder Sarabia’s Espanyol win at San Mamés

Espanyol beat Athletic Club 1-0 in Bilbao through a Roberto Fernández goal. The result extends a strong run since Manolo González left and leaves Athletic seventh after a home defeat in which they dominated the statistics.

A crowd of 46,107 was at San Mamés on Friday 20 November 2026. The fixture opened Matchday 13 of LaLiga EA Sports.

The win was Eder Sarabia’s second in charge of Espanyol and his second in a row away from home. The club have now taken seven of the nine points available since González left, according to EFE. Espanyol named Sarabia head coach on 28 October 2026, on a contract that runs until 2028.

His appointment followed a 4-3 Copa del Rey defeat at Sestao River. A 1-0 win at Villarreal, a 0-0 draw with Deportivo La Coruna and Friday’s victory in Bilbao make up Espanyol’s results since González’s exit. Their goal difference now stands at zero.

The first half ended goalless. Tyrhys Dolan replaced Pere Milla in the 57th minute. Sarabia also sent on Gabriel Moscardó and Javi Hernández in the 65th minute.

A minute later, Dolan set up Fernández for the winner. It was the striker’s sixth league goal of the season, putting him eighth in the LaLiga scoring list. He finished with 3 shots and a rating of 7.92.

Sarabia then brought on Unai Núñez and Javi Puado in the 84th minute to protect the lead. Clemens Riedel was booked in the third minute of stoppage time, Espanyol’s only card of the night.

Goalkeeper Ángel Fortuño made six saves to keep a clean sheet.

The result gave Espanyol a third successive league win over Athletic. They won 2-0 at home on 13 May 2026 and 2-1 at San Mamés on 22 December 2025.

Athletic controlled most of the statistics. They had 58% of possession and 9 corners to Espanyol’s 2. On target, the hosts had 6 efforts and the visitors 3.

Edin Terzić moved away from the 4-4-2 he had used in previous matches to fit Oihan Sancet into a 4-2-3-1. The change did not produce more attacking threat. Deia judged this to be Athletic’s worst performance at San Mamés since Terzić took charge.

Nico Williams had 5 shots and 3 key passes. Iñigo Ruiz de Galarreta also created 3 chances in 29 minutes on the pitch. Athletic collected three yellow cards, for Iñaki Williams, Ruiz de Galarreta and Yeray Álvarez.

Athletic fall to defeat at San Mames.#AthleticEspanyol #AthleticClub 🦁 pic.twitter.com/tRnTpjuX14

— Athletic Club (@Athletic_en) November 20, 2026

Before kick-off, San Mamés paid tribute to Elene Gurtubay and Daniela Agote, who won the Under-20 World Cup.

After 12 matches, Terzić’s side have 16 points. Their recent run reads one draw, two wins and one defeat in the league before Friday’s loss. Real Sociedad sit fifth on 22 points.

Athletic travel to bottom side Malaga on Saturday 28 November. Espanyol host Getafe on Monday 30 November.

#1137. How Louisville City plans to tackle rare morning kickoff vs. Sacramento Republic in Saturday's USL final

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

In recent years, Louisville City FC have been one of the most successful regular-season teams in United Soccer League history, but it hasn't translated to winning the big game. They haven't won the USL Championship since 2018, and while this season has been a trying time dealing with injuries and a new coach taking over, they're playing their best soccer when it matters to set up a strange clash with Sacramento Republic at noon Eastern on Saturday. What's strange isn't that it's Louisville and Sacramento meeting, but that the match kicks off at 9 a.m. local time, a time Louisville forward Ray Serrano says he hasn't played soccer at since he was 15. While it's a regular training time for Louisville and they'll try to keep things on an East Coast timeline, it's hard not to take the shift into account when planning for a final.

It's a challenge that comes with the desire to reach as many fans as possible with a final of this magnitude. Leagues have to work with broadcast networks to ensure that the slots work, and for the USL, having the game on CBS is worth the risk of a 9 a.m. local start with a West Coast team hosting. It's nothing Louisville won't be prepared for, as they look to keep their internal clocks on Eastern Standard Time.

"No, we're trying to stay on Eastern Time, so for us, it's training time," defender Kyle Adams said. "Wake up at 8:00 a.m., but really it's 5:00 a.m. Go to sleep a little bit earlier. Try to do everything really just to stay on Eastern Time, eat a little bit earlier on the night before, and just treat it as going into training, and then get after them."

Other teams have dealt with similar issues, like the Los Angeles Rams when playing an NFL game in Australia, but it's still a struggle to deal with en route to a cup final as Louisville look to reach the pinnacle of the sport for the first time since 2018. Winners of the Prinx Tires USL Cup during the regular season, they do have cup experience that will prove to be fruitful in this competition, which Adams noted has been something that brings the injury-riddled squad together. "We know in the last few years we've struggled in these knockout games, but this year we've turned it on," Serrano said. "It has been really good preparation, just the mentality of going into them, how we deal with the pressure, and we're seeing the fruits of all that now."

It's cliche to say that because of the adversity that they've dealt with, the club is playing its best soccer when it matters, but between using four goalkeepers during the season and seeing manager Danny Cruz depart to be an assistant manager with Minnesota United, it hasn't been an easy task for interim manager Simon Bird to get this team on the right track at this critical juncture.

"Going back to the main part is the adversity that we've faced. You mentioned injuries, having to deal with that side of it, some of the various parts of the season, different things we've had to deal with from a tactical or technical standpoint, where we've lost games, and we feel that we shouldn't have lost games," Bird said when reflecting on the team's development under his leadership. "The most impressive thing I said to the guys today, yesterday in training, we worked on our defensive structure, but the whole training session I thought was excellent, not just the defensive side, off the ball but with the ball, and to see it all come together towards the end of the season is really rewarding. Hopefully, we can carry that on and put together a complete performance, and that's what we've had throughout the season-moments where we've let ourselves down in all these different areas, set pieces, maybe transition at other times, in front of goal. So, putting it all together for a complete performance on Saturday is the goal."

Traveling away to a tough environment in Heart Health Park, Louisville will meet the hottest team in the league in Sacramento Republic. They've ridden a club-record 16-game unbeaten run to the final based on their defense. That has set a strong foundation to build on, and it could make the final one where the first team to score a goal wins the match. Sacramento's squad also has experience in USL Cup finals, which goes a long way when preparing for games of this stature.

"I don't think it can hurt to have that. This would be a step forward for my first final. I think experience is invaluable for players and for staff," Sacramento coach Neil Collins said. "But then there's also the recognition that every game is different, every team is different, and every season is different. So it's just trying to get the balance right and enjoy the opportunity. You've got to have the mechanisms to control the things you can control. Obviously, the opposition team is trying to do the same, and we've got to do everything we can to be ready to take the opportunity when it comes. But the experience will definitely help us; there's plenty of that in our dressing room."

It's a final where the best that the league has to offer will be on display, and it couldn't come at a better time. The summer of soccer, with the United States hosting the World Cup alongside Mexico and Canada, has truly turned into a soccer avalanche, and this final showcases one of the top atmospheres in the league. You can't ask for much better than that, as no matter what, a drought will come to an end. Sacramento Republic haven't won the final since 2014, while Louisville haven't won since 2018, and for these clubs, it will mean a lot to get back to the top.

#1136. Espí’s late winner seals ninth straight win as Real Madrid draw level with Barcelona

Substitute Carlos Espí struck late as Real Madrid came from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 at the Santiago Bernabéu. The result keeps Madrid firmly in the title race with Barcelona.

The victory over Celta on Saturday 21 November 2026 was Madrid’s ninth in a row. It also kept their 100% home record this season intact.

The winner began with a Vinícius Júnior cross. Espí headed it, Celta goalkeeper Ionuț Radu saved, and the striker scored from the rebound in the six-yard box. He had been on the pitch for only a few minutes.

Espí had played only 44 minutes of LaLiga football this season before kick-off, according to ESPN. All three of his league goals have now won games, against Espanyol, Elche and Celta. He also scored in the 4-3 Champions League comeback win at Roma. The goal was his fourth of the season, the club said.

Espí called his first goal in front of the Bernabéu crowd his most special for the club. José Mourinho described him as a pure penalty-box striker. The coach added that football history has many players like him who decide games without playing many minutes.

Pablo Durán gave Celta a sixth-minute lead from a Williot Swedberg pass. Kylian Mbappé then missed a penalty in the 39th minute, and the visitors led 1-0 at the break.

Mourinho had started Vinícius and Federico Valverde on the bench. He sent them on with Marc Cucurella in the second half to chase the game. Thibaut Courtois kept Madrid in it with a strong low save from a long-range Durán shot in the 65th minute. A minute later, Jude Bellingham equalised from an Mbappé assist.

The figures show how one-sided the contest was. Madrid had 24 shots to Celta’s 8 and an expected goals total of 3.8 against 1.52. Radu made five saves, and the hosts held 64% of possession.

Celta coach Claudio Giráldez said Madrid’s substitutes had decided the game. He pointed out that he had started six academy graduates. Many of his players were appearing at the Bernabéu for the first time. Giráldez replaced Hugo Álvarez with Ferran Jutglà at half-time and sent on Iago Aspas for Durán in the 76th minute. Celta are 13th on 13 points.

Barcelona still top the table on goal difference, 35 to 22. They can move clear again when they host Villarreal on Sunday 22 November.

In the LaLiga scoring chart, Mbappé is second with 13 goals. Barcelona’s Raphinha leads on 15.

📞 Just call Carlos Espí. #LaLigaHighlights pic.twitter.com/z9KqjfkhmY

— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) November 21, 2026

Earlier on Saturday, Rafael Nadal was elected to Real Madrid’s board of directors at an Extraordinary General Assembly at Ciudad Real Madrid. Later, he watched the game from the stands and was visibly emotional.

#1135. NWSL, U.S. Soccer continue focus on women's soccer growth with player and executive development programs

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – The NWSL has always been a measuring stick for the growth of women's soccer in the U.S., which in recent years has been headlined by skyrocketing expansion fees and increased fan engagement. There's a buzzword that continues to pop up around the league, one that is rarely associated with the key performance indicators – pipeline. After she read out another list of attendance figures and viewership numbers before the 2026 season wraps up with Saturday's NWSL Championship (8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+), commissioner Jessica Berman made a hard pivot in her state of the league remarks on Thursday to say the league is officially in the business of prioritizing said pipeline.

In the first of four announcements she teased was in service of that. The NWSL announced two initiatives on Thursday: the creation of a player development rule (PDR) and a sporting executive leadership program, designed specifically to focus on the foundation of the league's structure. The plans are a marriage of the league's business model and sporting objectives, a tacit understanding that the two go hand-in-hand, especially for a league that is admittedly driven by star power. These new plans, though, are hardly the only initiatives that will influence the pipeline.

The NWSL's new initiatives reflect a shifting focus across the American soccer landscape, one that seems driven by the heightened interest in the sport courtesy of this year's World Cup in North America. The league's financial stability enabled this shift but beyond that, there are overlapping commitments across the industry to finally fix one of American soccer's most evident problems – the pipeline. The sport's success in this country has often come in spite of a fractured youth soccer system, one that U.S. Soccer hopes to unite in the coming years.

The parties, be it in conjunction or individually, are also dead set on ensuring the women's game is held in equal regard to the men's every step of the way.

The PDR joins a list of NWSL rules in recent years that have incentivized clubs to recruit young players more easily such as the U-18 Entry Mechanism and organizing its first-ever combine last year. The new rule requires participating clubs to develop a curriculum that supports player development and is tied directly to salary cap relief.

"What can we do at the league to motivate and incentivize clubs to develop players?" Sarah Gregorius, the NWSL's vice president of sporting, told CBS Sports. "What do we have in our toolkit? And one of the things we obviously have in our toolkit is a salary cap and we can use that as a motivation and as an incentive to encourage the types of behavior around player development that we want to see, and hopefully, it's really our first structural foray into player development. Again, it's deliberately an incentive. It's not a mandate. It's up to the clubs. If they want to participate, if they want to access the reward, they know what they have to do in order to do that."

There is a perceived industry standard about developing young players, even if it is as far from an exact science as it gets. Academy systems tied to clubs are how players often come up the ranks – that is true across the men's game including in MLS and increasingly so for women's players in Europe. The NWSL does not have a streamlined system that mirrors the academy set-up and interestingly enough, is not actually trying to go in that direction.

"This is a pretty unique country," Gregorius said. "It doesn't actually work to pick something up from overseas and plop it down over here and I'm actually not convinced in the two years that I've spent here and everything that I've learned that this vertical academy system across the clubs makes the most sense. There's already a ton of incredible player development happening. There's just a bit of a lack of cohesion and a lack of connection to the professional game … The Spanish model won't work here, the German model wouldn't work here, the Japanese model wouldn't work here. Got a ton of respect for what they're doing in their countries but the reason that it works is it's for those countries. We have to do something that works for this one, which has characteristics that no other country in the world has. F---, this place is big. It's dynamic. There's a lot going on."

Gregorius believes a league-issued mandate might further fracture an already splintered landscape.

"If I think about it from a local level, some of our clubs are in markets that have thriving youth ecosystems, right?" Gregorius started. "So if all of a sudden there was a mandate from the league that every single club – which is what they do in England – has to come in and have a professional game academy, they're going to all of a sudden have to start pulling players out of those environments, which is disruptive for the kids. It's disruptive for the families. Some of those kids and families are also fans of the team. It's the icing on the cake in those particular markets so all of a sudden, you create tension. You create tension for the parents. You create tension for the kids. You create tension within the fan groups. They're like, 'Well, no, actually. You've stripped out my youth club in order to service a mandate from the league, not paying attention to the fact that all of your talented players have come through the system.' That's not what we want. That's bad for player development and it's bad for fan engagement, to be honest."

The NWSL is distinguishing itself from MLS, a league to which it has no formal ties but one that committed to the traditional academy system over a decade ago and can count it amongst its greatest successes. There's no stigma associated with the diverging path, though – U.S. Soccer has committed to viewing the women's game specifically through a female lens in recent years, an initiative championed by U.S. women's national team head coach Emma Hayes but embraced by many, either through her influence or separate from it.

"The intense focus on the pathway is very intentional," U.S. Soccer COO Dan Helfrich told CBS Sports. "The intense focus as we build the next version of the women and girls pathway, that it's done through a female lens, is very intentional and look, there is going to be, we believe, historic investment and interest in women's soccer and it's it's going to crescendo into the 2031 World Cup and making sure we take advantage of this moment to corral and direct the investment and interest in a sustainable way. I don't think there's anything that could have a greater legacy for women's soccer in our country than that."

The distinction between the men's and women's games, even at the youth levels, is easy for Helfrich to make because they have always existed.

"The first thing is the environments for players to develop in," he said. "it's really important that they're tailored to women and girl  and that includes environments for youth clubs and colleges and professional clubs and so some of the work, for example, of the Kang Women's Institute becomes really important to do the research to develop the insights and then for us to promulgate them into all these areas, that's different and if you look at the as-is state of the pathway, the league structures for girls are different than the league structures for boys. The role of college soccer for girls is different than the role of college soccer for boys and so practically, if you're trying to optimize a future, you apply a different lens."

There's more shared consensus when it comes to developing leaders that will foster players' growth, which is where the sporting executive leadership program kicks in. The program is built around specialized education for sporting director types, the first yearlong edition of the initiative already in session. A cohort of six – Haley Carter of the Washington Spirit, Caitlin Carducci of the Orlando Pride, Angela Mangano of the Houston Dash, Jeff Agoos of the Portland Thorns, Kelly Cousins of the Utah Royals and Dome Guasch of the Boston Legacy – already took part in their first session of a project supported both by U.S. Soccer and FIFA.

"The 16, now 18, individuals who hold the highest sporting position at the clubs have an outsized impact on the on-field identity and on-field product of their club so therefore, all of those people have an an impact on the on-field product of the league," Gregorius noted. "It's also, curiously enough, one of the few roles within the sporting department that doesn't have a license. You don't need to have completed a particular license. There's no education requirements or anything like that so when we also did an audit of the 16 clubs and who was holding those positions, some have former players, some have lawyers, some have people with an operations background, some have people with a coaching background. It was very varied so we're like, okay, if we know that this group has a ton of impact, if we know that they don't go through any structured learning. Is there a way that we can wrap our arms around them and support them?"

The uniqueness of this program is that it is tied specifically to the NWSL, which operates independently of a men's league unlike some of its European counterparts or even the WNBA.

"It's the first of its kind because every other f---ing part of the world just cares about men's football so we're really, really proud of not only the commitment and the discipline around trying to get it off the ground," Gregorius said.

It is in parallel with other initiatives the league and U.S. Soccer have worked on in recent years. The NWSL combine, for example, was also an effort to bolster female coaches while U.S. Soccer frequently uses its new national training center to conduct coaching courses with the youth game in mind.

"What I would say is to grow the game the way it needs to be grown, we can't underestimate or overlook the non-player part of development," Helfrich said, "and the non-player part of development is coaches. The non-player part of development is scouts. Non-player part of development is referees and the non-player part of development is front office, technical leaders and so, building a partnership with the NWSL on all of those important non-player development activities is a big priority."

The NWSL's partnership with U.S. Soccer on this program also speaks to a unique truth about American soccer. The women's game is held in incredibly high regard in the U.S. because of the historic success of the USWNT, who have four World Cup titles and five Olympic gold medals in their 40-year history. The USWNT's reputation of being serial winners is intrinsically tied to the health of the federation, the NWSL and in some ways, American soccer as a whole.

"Honest to God, I've loved waking up every day and only thinking about the women's game," Gregorius, a former New Zealand international, said. "It's brilliant and it's very unique over here that we are able to do that and what I love about working with U.S. Soccer, as well, to be honest, is they're the same. They're almost more interested in the women's game sometimes than they are anything else … It's an organization that is already on the train, you know what I mean? The NWSL and our clubs, it's not even a question of being in the shadow of the men's game or any of that other bulls--- that you kind of encounter in other places. The focus is unwavering and that's brilliant."

#1134. Arsenal nous frustrates Liverpool as 14-year Anfield hoodoo ends with statement win

It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

Few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

“The mission was something we didn’t complete in 14 years,” Mikel Arteta said, having famously – in an Amazon documentary series – played You’ll Never Walk Alone to his players as they walked out to train to try and overcome a perceived mental block.

“There are reasons for that. Some of it psychological, some of it moments we did not nail on the pitch,” the Arsenal manager added of the winless run.

The result means that the north Londoners have already now won away at Villa Park, the Stadium of Light, the City Ground and Anfield. Stadiums where they dropped points last season. And that feels ominous.

A win would maybe have thrust Liverpool into the title race. Instead, under Andoni Iraola, and with an evolving young team – with promising 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni handed his league debut – they are already nine points behind after just nine matches.

It is also clear, however, that they could have prevented this defeat having somehow been denied a first-half penalty after Alexander Isak’s shirt was blatantly pulled by Jurrien Timber as the striker tried to head home a cross.

Referee Andy Madley may have missed it, but what was the excuse of Stuart Attwell, the VAR? It was a stunningly poor decision – another bad day for Pro Ref and the use of technology.

It might be argued that Timber did not pull hard enough to prevent Isak from reaching the ball. But the defender grabbed the shirt and continued to hold it for a long time. It had to be a penalty. Little wonder Iraola said Isak should dive next time. Who can blame him?

What is also clear and obvious is that, once again, Arsenal’s resilience, defensive determination and appetite for toughing it out will be their greatest weapons. They are certainly, under Arteta, not here to win friends – just to win matches and trophies.

“That defensive line, that togetherness we have is undefeated. It’s something I have never seen before,” Declan Rice, who was also a stand-out performer and delivered a fine assist for the winner, said.

Arsenal’s version of the Yellow Wall was, indeed, hugely impressive – it is now six clean sheets from their nine league games and, despite all their pressure, Liverpool did not have a shot on target. That has never happened in the Premier League since such statistics started to be compiled in 2003 (422 games ago).

“That’s incredible. It did not feel like it on the pitch. Again, it’s the commitment of every single player,” Arteta said. And that was indisputable.

Even the expected second-half momentum, the expected surge of attack after attack as Liverpool faced the Kop, crashed on Arsenal’s back line. The visitors were so well-drilled that they stifled space – they refused to crumble.

Arsenal put their bodies on the line with blocks and tackles and a bit of time-wasting. There were dark arts, especially from both centre-halves with Gabriel going unpunished after claiming he was struck in the face by Isak early on – VAR anyone? – and the otherwise outstanding Ezri Konsa throwing himself to the ground after minimal contact from the Liverpool centre-forward.

In fairness there was also a bit of that from an increasingly frustrated Liverpool with Alexis Mac Allister going down after touching heads with Noni Madueke, having already tried to provoke Martin Odegaard with a hand to the head when the Arsenal captain was on the turf. That was not good from Mac Allister either.

And the only goal? Again, more frustration for Liverpool. It was well-constructed from Arsenal, but only after Alisson Becker’s loose goal kick, aimed towards Jérémy Jacquet, who was slow to react, was intercepted by Odegaard with Bruno Guimarães poking the ball to the right, where it was collected by Madueke.

There was an overlap by Rice and his low centre was precise and dangerous across the face of the six-yard area, with Virgil van Dijk unsure what to do. It ran beyond the far post where Kai Havertz side-footed home.

"Absolutely brilliant from Arsenal." Kai Havertz gives Arsenal an early lead at Anfield! ⚡️ https://t.co/eeyhRcLlel

After that? Liverpool swarmed over Arsenal, particularly in the first-half with Florian Wirtz’s free-kick cannoning back off the crossbar and Mac Allister somehow heading over. He was six yards out and unmarked, it was a glorious chance.

That was the hosts’ last tangible opportunity to score. As well as Arsenal defended, it was not a good afternoon for Liverpool’s forwards, Bradley Barcola in particular, although it was interesting to see Arsenal double-up on Rio Ngumoha when he came on. Arteta reacted by bringing on a second left-back, in Piero Hincapié.

Both of Atlético’s first-half goals in this matchday 13 LaLiga fixture came inside the opening 30 minutes.

#1132. NWSL Championship 2026 picks: Will the Washington Spirit or the Kansas City Current reach the top?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

For the third straight time, the Washington Spirit are playing for the NWSL Championship. The No. 3 Spirit host the No. 4 Kansas City Current at Audi Field on Saturday for the biggest prize in domestic women's soccer. Kickoff is at 8 p.m. ET, and you can see it all on CBS and Paramount+.

The Washington Spirit won it all in 2021 but came up just short in each of the last two finals. This may be the day that Trinity Rodman gets her second crown.

The Kansas City Current bring plenty to the final and may just be the favorites. They're back in the big game for the first time since 2022 after ending NJ/NY Gotham FC's title defense in the semis. Croix Bethune, who used to play for the Spirit, curled in a free-kick stunner, and Haley Hopkins won it in the 89th minute.

So who lifts the trophy? Our experts make their picks below.

Star-studded attack: This year's finalists did not have the most straightforward journeys to the NWSL Championship, but the good news for each of them is that there will be few excuses when they finally take to the pitch on Saturday. Trinity Rodman is about to cap off a career-best campaign after an injury-riddled 2025 season and will be joined by the impactful Sofia Cantore and midseason arrival Clara Luvanga, putting the Washington Spirit in as good a position as any to come out with a win that has eluded them over the last two seasons. The Current, though, are in the same boat --  they have struggled without their all-star trio, but each of Croix Bethune, Temwa Chawinga and Michelle Cooper will be available on Saturday and equally capable of turning the game in their favor.

Midfield battles: There's going to be a real display of veteran prowess and eager energy. Both teams have experienced players and rising stars, and it'll be a combo of chess and tug of war during the NWSL Championship. Washington Spirit's Andi Sullivan anchors most things in the middle, with Leicy Santos linking play and Melissa Bethi's recent rise in form. Even with all the changes from injuries to departures and returns from maternity leave, the Spirit are gelling at a good time in a crucial part of the pitch. They'll battle against Kansas City's Lo'eau LaBonta and Vanessa DiBernardo, two of the best in the league with longevity and finesse. Ball knowers understand that they're two players who can control a game, close and create lanes, or serve up goals and assists. Add attacking mid Croix Bethune into the mix, and Kansas City have plenty of ways to win the middle of the park.  -- Sandra Herrera

Balance: At their best, the Washington Spirit are a side who can win a game in multiple ways, and while there's plenty of star power on both sides, balance is where they win out. It's a fascinating match for both sides and one where the margins will be thin but being able to have a strong attack led by Trinity Rodman along with a buildup that Andi Sullivan keeps control of. If the Spirit can control the pace, it will be a long day for Kansas City but Croix Bethune will have ideas of her own as well.  -- Chuck Booth

Washington Spirit: The Spirit have tossed around the phrase that the third time's the charm after two empty-handed trips to the NWSL Championship and this year, it's hard not to buy the argument. Rodman is happy and healthy but she is just one part of a team that has been smartly assembled over the years and seems as cohesive as ever. -- Pardeep Cattry

Washington Spirit: Truthfully, the pressure is on the Washington Spirit headed into this one, and that typically doesn't play out the best for teams who are the higher seed or considered favorites on paper. Kansas City will be a more than worthy opponent, but the Spirit's third time in the final comes with a long home build-up through and back to Audi Field, and any mental component needed will come with a boost from the crowd environment. -- Sandra Herrera

Washington Spirit: Sure, this is a "neutral" venue, but being a home team in a final match will carry the Spirit at Rowdy Audi. Considering that this is the third consecutive final, fans snatched up tickets as soon as they could, assuming that the home side would be here. While all the pressure is on the Spirit and rightfully so, the team has also embraced that, and once the first goal goes in the net, this is going to turn into a party.  -- Chuck Booth

Trinity Rodman: Is this an obvious choice? Yes, yes it is, but to be fair, Rodman has earned the right to be the easy pick. She has always been key to the Spirit's success but hit a new level this season, to the point that she had a very valid MVP case even if her ex-teammate Ashley Sanchez took it home instead after a record-breaking season with the North Carolina Courage. Rodman's ability to create and score chances means she's very likely to have a say on Saturday, one that could very well end the Spirit's five-year wait for another championship. -- Pardeep Cattry

Clara Luvanga: The last few NWSL Championship MVPs have gone to the lone goal scorer. Barbra Banda won it in 2024 for her game-winning goal, and Rose Lavelle earned it for her single title goal in 2025. If these two teams match up on the pitch as evenly as they do on paper, then it could come down to a single moment again, and Luvanga has shown she's better positioned for it with her current form. Her four goals and three assists through seven games make her an efficient threat on goal, and could finally be the difference maker for the group in their third final. -- Sandra Herrera

Trinity Rodman: To win finals, you need your best players to be at their best. All eyes have been on Trinity Rodman this season after she became the highest-paid player in NWSL history, and she has delivered. Considering that the next development in her career is to become a player for the biggest moments, and capping off the final by scoring will be just the way to do it. -- Chuck Booth

#1131. Welcome to the Man United madhouse, Mauricio! Man United emerge from the chaos at Sporting Lisbon with a draw as Senne Lammens joins their band of self-saboteurs in game that had it all, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 17:18 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 19:22 EST, 25 November 2026

A week into the job and Mauricio Pochettino must be getting used to the madness of Manchester United by now.

If it's not drones flying over the training ground, red card controversies and random divots of grass, it's his own players shooting themselves in the foot.

At least, Pochettino emerged from the craziness in Lisbon with a draw on a night when Bruno Fernandes celebrated his return to the Jose Alvalade Stadium with a couple of goals.

But these are the kind of nights that must drive coaches like Pochettino potty. After the carnage of Michael Carrick's final two games in charge against Roma and Aston Villa, and the rancour of the Argentine's introduction to the Old Trafford circus at Anfield on Sunday, this was another mad, mad spectacle.

Where do we start? The two acts of self-sabotage by goalkeeper Senne Lammens? United's two disallowed goals? The first was harsh on the scorer, Amad Diallo, but also Youri Tielemans who received a booking that led to his sending-off in injury-time. Or maybe that divot, which Fernandes claimed he created and then hit to put United ahead with a bizarre deflected goal?

At the end of all the chaos, United had conceded five penalties in their last five games and picked up four red cards.

Senne Lammens (left) two errors cost Man United a deserving win at Sporting as they drew

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino comforts Lammens at full-time after his mistakes

That is not something that will sit well with Pochettino. But after venting his frustration with the officiating over Leny Yoro's sending-off at Anfield, which dominated the build-up to this game after it was rescinded, here was another sequence of events that seemed to conspire against him.

It's not as if the Jose Alvalade Stadium was a cauldron of emotion to scramble the senses of the two sets of players and match officials either. Fernandes got a polite round of applause from the fans and a framed memento from his old club before kick-off.

When the teams came out, he was one of three former United players alongside Cristiano Ronaldo and Luis Nani honoured on a tifo of the Sporting Lisbon greats.

It was all very flat until the half-hour mark when United self-imploded again. Geny Catamo picked up the ball on the edge of the United box and teased Lisandro Martinez, playing at left back.

Martinez took the bait and stuck his leg out. He barely caught Sporting's No 10 and it took Catamo a full second to realise he had, before going down theatrically and earning a very soft penalty from Polish referee Szymon Marciniak.

Sporting's top scorer Luis Suarez stepped up and made it easy for Lammens to make the save. It was a let-off for United and potentially a big moment in a difficult season for Lammens.

But he undid his good work 75 seconds later when Maxi Araujo chased a long ball over the top pursued by Noussair Mazraoui. For some reason, Lammens thought it would be a good idea to race 25 yards out of his goal.

Araujo stepped inside the Belgium goalkeeper and went down under his clumsy challenge. Marciniak pointed to the spot again, and this time Suarez made no mistake.

Lammens started positively saving this Luis Suarez penalty before conceding a spot-kick

Yet, minutes later Suarez scored after being given a second penalty following Lammens error

United thought they had eqaulised before half-time but Amad Diallo's header was ruled out for a percieved foul in the build-up by Youri Tielemans that earned him a booking

After all the upset over the officiating at Anfield, United were on the wrong end of another big call just before half-time here when Tielemans stretched to poke the ball through to Diallo and inadvertently caught Goncalo Inacio who went down claiming serious injury.

Goalkeeper Kaique Pereira saved Diallo's first effort and Marciniak blew his whistle for a foul before the Ivorian headed in at the second attempt so there was no opportunity for VAR to review it. The referee booked Tielemans, but there was a strong argument that it wasn't even a foul.

United re-emerged for the second half undeterred and hit back to score twice through Fernandes within five minutes of the restart.

The United captain played the ball through for Martinez and then converted from the spot after his team-mate went down in a tangle of legs with Eduardo Quaresma.

Bruno Fernandes levelled for United just after half-time when they were awarded a penalty

He then put them ahead with this left-footed shot that hit a divot on the pitch before flying in

United's lead was undone late on when Lammens' second major error allowed Suarez to score

United's evening was compounded when Tielemans was sent off late on for a second yellow

Two minutes later, and having made the divot turning in the penalty box 17 seconds earlier, Fernandes somehow managed to hit it with a hopeful effort from 25 yards. Pereira had the ball covered but it took an outrageous deflection just outside the six-yard box and flew through his arms.

But this is United and nothing is straightforward. In the 80th minute, with victory within their grasp, Lammens had all the time in the world to catch a high ball from Ivan Fresneda. Perhaps too long. Unforgivably, he dropped it in front of Suarez who hooked into the net.

There was still time for more drama when United had another goal from a Fernandes' corner chalked off for Patrick Dorgu's foul on Pereira, after VAR sent Marciniak to the monitor, and he then showed Tielemans a second yellow card.

Pochettino looked on frustrated and probably as confused as the rest of us.

#1130. Cucho Hernández heads both goals as Betis win 2-0 at Slovan Bratislava to go fourth

Two headers from Cucho Hernández gave Real Betis victory over Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League. The result strengthens Manuel Pellegrini's side's position in the league phase with three rounds left.

For Hernández, Tuesday night was his first start after more than a month out injured, and he marked it with a double in Bratislava. The win came in the fifth round of the Champions League league stage.

Ángel Ortiz supplied the cross for the opener, delivering it from the right for Hernández to meet at the back post. Isco then supplied the assist for his second after the break. That goal was his third of Betis’s Champions League campaign.

Hernández went off after 63 minutes, and Troy Parrott took his place. Marc Roca replaced Facundo Bernal, who had been booked in the seventh minute. Álvaro Fidalgo came on for Isco.

Pellegrini made six changes from the side that drew 1-1 with Sevilla in the derby. Isco, Abde and Antony kept their places.

The visitors dominated the game in every department. Betis completed 605 of their 670 passes, an accuracy of 90%. Slovan managed 309 passes in total. Betis put six shots on target, while Slovan managed two. The expected goals figure was 1.52 for Betis and 0.43 for the hosts.

Slovan goalkeeper Dominik Takáč made four saves. At the other end, Álvaro Vallés made a sharp save to stop Andraž Šporar, a moment UEFA’s match summary named as one of the key moments of the game. French referee Jérôme Brisard showed one yellow card to each side.

The game also brought Slovan coach Yaya Touré up against Pellegrini, his old manager at Manchester City. Touré’s side stay bottom of the table after five defeats. They have conceded 19 goals and scored only one.

Betis now have four wins and one defeat from five matches. They are well placed to fight for a top-eight finish over the last three rounds, according to AFP. A place in the top eight would send them straight into the last 16 without a play-off.

The remaining fixtures are demanding. Betis host Como on 9 December 2026 and Arsenal on 20 January 2027. They finish the league phase away to Bayern Munich on 27 January 2027.
